title: 2027 1L Summer Associate
description:
About AbbVie
AbbVie's mission is to discover and deliver innovative medicines and solutions that solve serious health issues today and address the medical challenges of tomorrow. We strive to have a remarkable impact on people's lives across several key therapeutic areas including immunology, oncology and neuroscience - and products and services in our Allergan Aesthetics portfolio. For more information about AbbVie, please visit us at  www.abbvie.com . Follow @abbvie on  LinkedIn,   Facebook ,  Instagram ,  X  and  YouTube.
2027 Overview
Summer associates will be immersed in AbbVie’s in-house legal and compliance teams, learning about and handling real-world matters under the supervision of AbbVie attorneys and compliance officers. Summer associates will work with one of the following departments within the in-house legal or compliance team for the duration of the summer internship:
Patent Legal Academy
Work on a wide variety of patent prosecution and IP (patent, trade secret) litigation-related tasks, which may include drafting materials for U.S. and foreign patent prosecution, listing patents in the FDA’s Orange Book, analyzing freedom-to-operate issues, addressing contractual issues, evaluating issues related to biopharmaceutical patent and trade secret litigation, and participating in strategy meetings with in-house and outside prosecution and litigation counsel.
Clinical R&D Legal Academy
Work on a wide range of clinical trial-related legal and regulatory matters in support of AbbVie’s therapeutic pipeline. Provides support for AbbVie’s global clinical research-based pharmaceutical business, including: clinical trial design; executing transactions required to get a clinical trial up and running, conducting legal analysis relating to patient-related matters such as informed consent, recruitment and retention strategies, and integration of novel technologies into AbbVie’s clinical trials; and providing global regulatory advice relating to AbbVie’s pipeline programs.
Corporate Legal Academy
Work in key corporate legal areas such as corporate financing, securities compliance and disclosure, compensation and benefits, and corporate governance.
Strategic Transactions Academy
Substantive legal work related to acquisition transactions as well as new and existing collaborations; assessing antitrust risks associated with mergers, acquisitions, and licensing transactions; and venture capital transactions.
Global Commercial Legal Academy
Support comprehensive legal and strategic guidance to Marketing, Sales, Medical Affairs, and Regulatory Affairs teams. Advise on a broad range of matters involving the Food and Drug Administration (FDA), Federal Trade Commission (FTC), Office of Inspector General (OIG), and other applicable laws, regulations, and industry guidance relevant to our business.t various pharmaceutical and aesthetics brands by partnering with attorneys to deliver
Operations, Privacy, and Technology Academy
Support the Operations function, which is responsible for AbbVie’s product manufacturing, procurement of goods and services, quality assurance, supply chain, and various aspects of product development; support the Legal Privacy team; and work on various Legal Technology projects, including those related to AI and the use of data across the enterprise.
Litigation/Employment/Compliance Academy
Work alongside attorneys across AbbVie’s Commercial Litigation, Employment, Labor & Immigration, and Legal Compliance teams.  Opportunity to work across a broad array of litigation and counseling matters, including areas such as product liability, antitrust, contractual disputes, visa and other immigration issues, and compliance with relevant laws including the Anti-Kickback Statute, Food, Drug & Cosmetic Act, Foreign Corrupt Practices Act, and many others.
Office of Ethics and Compliance Academy
Gain hands-on experience by supporting the Compliance team in activities such as conducting policy assessments, developing and supporting training initiatives, monitoring business practices and participating in investigations to help promote compliant conduct under healthcare and pharmaceutical industry codes, laws, and regulations. This role will also involve cross-functional collaboration with teams in Operations, Commercial Brands, R&D, Privacy, and International.
***
All summer associates will research and present on a legal or compliance issue related to their work and will have the opportunity to meet and work with AbbVie’s in-house and outside counsel and compliance professionals, including partnering closely with both a manager and mentor who will both provide ongoing guidance and professional development.
By the end of the summer, AbbVie 1L Summer Associates should have attained:
practical experience working for a global biopharmaceutical company in an interesting and evolving area of law,
an understanding of how in-house attorneys and compliance officers provide value to their company as trusted advisors to the business,
leadership opportunities and experience building business relationships effectively, and
meaningful writing and communication development.
How to Apply
Submit your application, which includes your resume and related information at the AbbVie Career Site AND Email a single PDF consisting of the documents set forth below to AbbVieLegalAcademy@abbvie.com.
Current resume
A letter explaining your interest in the AbbVie 1L Legal Academy Program, including your ranking of your top three choices among the internship programs listed above.
A personal statement addressing how this program will be career transformative and enable you to be a leader within the legal profession or greater community
Undergraduate transcript (unofficial)
If applicable, other graduate transcripts (unofficial)
In addition, as soon as your first semester law school grades are available, please email your unofficial law school transcript to  abbvielegalacademy@abbvie.com .
Preference will be given to applications received by January 11, 2027.
Qualifications
Students must complete their 1L year at an ABA-accredited law school during 2026-2027
Must be enrolled in law school the semester following your internship
Strong undergraduate academic background, including in relevant disciplines
Statement regarding how this internship will be career transformative and enable you to be a leader within the legal profession or greater community

Drug Substance Engineering Internship Overview
Envision spending your summer working with energetic colleagues and inspirational leaders, all while gaining world-class experience in one of the most dynamic organizations in the pharmaceutical industry. This is a reality for AbbVie Interns.
Micronization of drug substance is a critical process in API manufacturing for ensuring downstream critical quality attributes. Micronization processes such as pin milling and jet milling leverage feed rate control to optimize the process performance, and while feed rate is well understood for many powder systems there is a gap in understanding the feed rate control of poorly flowing materials in micronization techniques.
The Drug Substance Engineering Intern within Product Development, Science, and Technology (PDS&T) will help establish a systematic approach to understand how the physical properties of powder systems impact their feeding performance in micronization processes.
Key responsibilities include:
Experimental studies to understand and characterize powder properties
Evaluate performance of micronization techniques (i.e. jet mill, pin mill) with various feed mechanisms
Analyze data and trends to identify signatures for process performance
Develop and verify computational models
Summarize and present findings in departmental and cross-functional settings
Minimum Qualifications
Currently enrolled in university, pursuing a PhD in Chemical Engineering, Materials Engineering, or other related field
Must be enrolled in university for at least one semester following the internship
Expected graduation date between December 2027 – June 2028
Preferred Qualifications
Exposure to comminution processes
Experience with physical characterization techniques (flowability, adhesion, cohesion, bulk density, laser diffraction particle size determination)
Proficient in computational modeling techniques (e.g., fluid dynamics, discrete element method)

2027 Formulation Sciences Internship Overview
Envision spending your summer working with energetic colleagues and inspirational leaders, all while gaining world-class experience in one of the most dynamic organizations in the pharmaceutical industry. This is a reality for AbbVie Interns.
Join AbbVie's Pharmaceutical Technology team within Product Development, Science, and Technology (PDS&T) to support late-stage formulation development for a solid oral dosage form. This internship focuses on investigating excipient compatibility, specifically the interaction between common solid oral excipients and chemical stability. The intern will work alongside experienced formulation scientists and analytical chemists to characterize this phenomenon and help define strategies to ensure robust, high-quality drug product formulations. The intern will also present findings to department leadership and potentially contribute to an external conference poster or publication.
Key responsibilities include:
Investigate the mechanism of excipient degradation in the presence of pH modifiers using appropriate analytical techniques (e.g., HPLC, titration and colorimetrical methods).
Collaborate on LC/MS analysis to identify and characterize leachable degradants associated with the implications to stabilizing the drug substance in the formulation.
Evaluate degradation kinetics under varying temperature and relative humidity conditions.
Assess potential mitigation strategies, including formulation and process variables.
Summarize experimental results and present findings and recommendations to the project team and department.

About AbbVie
AbbVie's mission is to discover and deliver innovative medicines and solutions that solve serious health issues today and address the medical challenges of tomorrow. We strive to have a remarkable impact on people's lives across several key therapeutic areas including immunology, oncology and neuroscience - and products and services in our Allergan Aesthetics portfolio. Position Summary
The Director, SOX Lifecycle & Enablement owns the end-to-end SOX program lifecycle for the enterprise and serves as the senior deputy within the IC SOX Center of Excellence. The role directs the annual risk assessment and scoping process, the risk and control matrix, the Section 302/404 certification process, and enterprise deficiency management, and coordinates the network of Business Unit SOX Leads across the organization. The Director also directly manages the U.S. business unit advisory portfolio (Commercial, Operations, and the Accounting Center of Excellence), the program’s highest-complexity areas, operating as a player-coach.
The role is central to a multi-year modernization of the SOX program, including the transition of management testing to an internal Testing & Analytics Hub, expanded automation and continuous monitoring, and an AI-enabled controls platform. During this transition, the Director is expected to be hands-on: directly managing stakeholder relationships, deficiency evaluations, and external auditor positions while building the operating rhythm of a maturing program. The change management and enablement mandate (training, communications, and adoption across control owners and BU SOX Leads) is an explicit part of the role.
Key Responsibilities
SOX Lifecycle Ownership
Direct the annual SOX risk assessment and scoping process, including materiality-driven scoping decisions and coordination with the external auditor on scope alignment.
Own the enterprise risk and control matrix: rationalization, updates for business and system change (acquisitions, ERP and data programs), and documentation quality standards.
Operate the Section 302/404 certification process, including quarterly sub-certifications and support for management’s quarterly and annual ICFR conclusions.
Own deficiency management as an enterprise process: intake, evaluation and severity assessment, aggregation analysis, remediation monitoring, and reporting for executive management and Audit Committee materials.
Manage external auditor (EY) coordination on scoping, reliance, and deficiency positions; prepare and defend management’s technical positions.
Business Unit Advisory
Directly manage the U.S. advisory portfolio (Commercial, Operations, Accounting Center of Excellence): control design consultation, readiness for business and system change, and first-line support to senior finance stakeholders.
Serve as the escalation point for significant deficiency assessments, contentious auditor matters, and issues bearing on quarterly certification conclusions across all business units.
Supervise and develop the Senior Manager responsible for the OUS and FSS advisory portfolio.
BU SOX Leads Network
Coordinate the enterprise network of Business Unit SOX Leads (approximately 12 business units): operating cadence, quarterly forums, standardized deficiency and change intake, and consistency of practice across units.
Change Management & Enablement
Lead training, communications, and adoption for program changes, including the Workiva-resident lifecycle, evidence standards, and continuous monitoring outputs as they deploy.
Oversee Workiva program administration (assessments, certifications, reporting) through the Senior Analyst, and partner with the AI & Analytics Enablement leader on platform direction.
Leadership
Manage and develop two direct reports; contribute to talent development across the Center of Excellence.
Partner with the Testing & Analytics Hub, AI & Analytics Enablement, and IT SOX leaders to operate an integrated program.
Qualifications
Required
Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, Information Systems, or a related field.
10+ years of progressive experience in audit and internal controls, with significant SOX program leadership at a large public company or serving large public company clients.
CPA or CIA (or equivalent certification).
Deep working knowledge of PCAOB AS 2201, the COSO 2013 framework, SEC Sections 302/404, and deficiency evaluation and aggregation practice.
Demonstrated experience managing external auditor relationships and defending technical positions.
Strong executive communication and stakeholder management skills with senior finance leadership.

Experience in pharmaceutical, life sciences, or other large multinational environments, including acquisition integration and ERP or data transformation programs.

title: Energy Analytics, TPM, Global Energy, Sustainability and Automation
description:
The Energy Analytics, Technical Program Manager (TPM) will scale power monitoring, insight generation, and energy and carbon reduction initiatives across Amazon's North America fulfillment operations. In this hands-on technical role, you will deploy and generate analysis from power metering infrastructure and implement load flexibility and energy optimization roadmaps that deliver measurable cost savings and carbon reductions. This work directly supports Amazon's demand-side power requirements and Climate Pledge commitments.
You will operate as an individual contributor, owning the delivery of defined and ambiguous work-streams while partnering with engineering, controls, data, operations and deployment teams to implement changes. You will influence cross-functional partners without authority, primarily at the team and management level, using data to drive decisions. You will integrate and analyze power metering information, providing load forecasts and generating cost and energy savings opportunities. Utility rate structures, time of day, demand ratchets and power factor penalties will influence your strategies. Technical assets influenced can include material handling, robotics, powered industrial trucks, lighting, heating ventilation and air conditioning, plug loads, electrical metering and more. Developed projects will be scaled across hundreds of facilities across the network, producing energy, cost and carbon benefit.
Key job responsibilities
● Build and execute technical solutions for energy and carbon reduction from pilot, data collection, through scaled implementation and measurement & verification (M&V) of results.  Energy and load optimization via control systems is a technical requirement: energy-conservation/standby modes, variable speed applications, and equipment scheduling.
● Drive continuous monitoring and energy efficiency improvements with Amazon's energy consuming assets.  Integrate power metering into our data sets, and develop analytics to identify opportunities, assess trending consumption changes, and measure benefits of conservation efforts.
● Prepare written analysis of feasibility studies and recommendations for various energy monitoring and power flexibility strategies.  Own metering data quality programs, check readings for completeness, outliers, and flag actionable improvements, and reconcile against known loads to ensure trusted insight generation.
● Develop metrics, baselines, and roadmaps that translate technical work into quantified outcomes (energy savings, cost savings or utility tariff arbitrage, load forecast, reliability, carbon reduction).
● Define and own technical approach and cross-system architecture for data configuration, standards and mechanisms for scalability and enforcement of key energy savings mechanisms. Decide how to build and prove new approaches managing tradeoffs for necessary business needs, rather than executing a defined scope.
● Manage projects against plans and objectives to ensure commitments are met, delivering against our power and Climate Pledge goals.
● Deep diving (troubleshooting) and unblocking issues that are prohibiting teams from pursuing energy reduction initiatives.
● Work with critical stakeholders on developing mechanisms for design standard integration for launching facilities that incorporate energy optimization procedures from Day 1.
● Analyze and communicate the financial impact of projects and initiatives (payback, return on investment, net present value)
● Serve as a technical reviewer for peers and partner engineers — reviewing control logic, metering architecture, and design-standard changes, and improving them on technical merit
● Quantify and own value add of energy savings mechanisms and how they reduce equipment runtime and increases reliability and lifespan.
● Calculate and report energy, water and carbon savings using International Performance Measurement and Verification Protocol methodologies.
● Manage multiple, complex projects simultaneously.
● Produce clear documentation, playbooks, and reporting that make work-streams repeatable.
A day in the life
You might spend the morning querying newly integrated power-metering data and validating it against the distribution-panel hierarchy — resolving a data-quality gap — then analyzing load profiles and build an energy-savings or peak-shaving model that quantifies the opportunity by equipment class. You then define network rollout suitability and prioritize these opportunities across sites. In the afternoon you develop control logic changes to implement an efficiency opportunity, propose updates to a design standard, or define a measurement method for implemented energy and cost savings to your stakeholders. You balance trade-offs between energy savings, technical complexity, equipment reliability, and cost — bringing well-reasoned recommendations and escalating the most ambiguous decisions for alignment.
About the team
The Global Energy, Sustainability and Automation (GESA) Energy team is dedicated to delivering energy efficiency, cost savings, and demand flexibility within Amazon's fulfillment network. We partner closely with design, controls, data, procurement, operations, field engineering, and deployment teams — as well as external vendors — to ensure our energy consumption is monitored and optimized. Our focus in the coming years is scaling our energy monitoring and analytics programs, expanding behavioral and retrofit programs, expanding load flexibility for power resilience and cost arbitrage benefit, and enhancing asset reliability and lifespan through efficient operation. If you are energized by large-scale technical challenges and want to make a tangible impact on energy use, this is the team for you.
Basic qualifications: - 5+ years of technical product or program management experience
- Bachelor's degree in engineering, computer science or equivalent
- Experience in SQL Server/MySQL, or experience in Redshift and experience in any Bigdata architecture
- Experience working with existing and emerging technologies related to building energy (i.e. power metering, conveyance, robotics, controls, HVAC, charging infrastructure)
Preferred qualifications: - Experience managing cross-functional programs and release schedules
- Familiarity with automation engineering and controls engineering concepts.
- Industry certifications: Certified Energy Manager, Certified Measurement & Verification Professional, Professional Engineer.

title: Senior Program Manager, Technology Supply Chain Organization Program Enablement
description:
Amazon's Technology Supply Chain is scaling, and the hardest part of that growth is getting an entire organization to change how it works. We are looking for a Senior Program Manager to own the change management discipline across Technology Supply Chain and make new ways of working the way the organization operates by default. You will design adoption approaches grounded in established change management methodologies such as Prosci/ADKAR and Kotter's 8-Step, build the communications that move behavior, and decide what to do when adoption stalls. You are comfortable in ambiguity and able to influence leaders and teams you do not manage. Success in this role is adoption: the standards you introduce become how teams actually operate. You will start with changes already in flight and build a discipline that applies to whichever change the organization adopts next. Over time the role grows. You will deepen expertise in change management and AI-assisted operations, and your scope will widen from driving individual changes to shaping how the whole organization absorbs change.
Key job responsibilities
- Own the change management discipline across Technology Supply Chain, partnering with leadership to shape the change strategy and owning its execution. Apply stakeholder analysis, readiness assessment, and resistance management to determine goals and design adoption approaches in ambiguous situations where the problem is not yet fully defined.
- Build adoption frameworks, playbooks, communications, and enablement materials that take each new way of working from something that exists to something the organization does by default, drawing on established change frameworks such as Prosci/ADKAR and Kotter.
- Partner with reporting, governance, and tooling teams to drive adoption of shared ways of working across all customer groups, influencing leaders and teams you do not directly manage to align on how the organization operates.
- Establish adoption measurement and reporting so progress and risk are visible before a change fails, own the judgment on how to respond when adoption stalls, and build the documentation and processes that make new ways of working durable beyond any single individual.
A day in the life
You spend your day building the organization's capacity to change. You partner with leadership to shape the change strategy, then own how it comes to life: assessing why change stalls and fixing it at the root rather than rescuing one rollout at a time. You coach leaders to be effective sponsors of the changes they own, because that is where change succeeds or fails. You sequence a portfolio of concurrent changes so the organization adopts them without saturating, and build the methodology and standards that let every team run change well. You work across every Technology Supply Chain group and influence leaders you do not manage. Your real product is not any single rollout. It is an organization that can change without breaking.
About the team
Technology Supply Chain delivers the full lifecycle of technology fulfillment for Amazon, sourcing, delivering, and deploying the hardware, infrastructure, and equipment that Amazon's Worldwide Stores operations and AWS data centers run on. As Amazon's technology footprint grows, Technology Supply Chain is the organization that keeps the supply chain behind it ahead of demand. Our team is the central program management and business operations function within Technology Supply Chain. Our principle is "enable rather than simply do": we take recurring programmatic work off every team through shared standards, processes, and tooling so each team can focus on the specialized work only it can do, and we build our own automation to do it.

title: AI/ML Engineer: System RF Data Ecosystem
description:
At Apple, new ideas quickly transform into products, services, and customer experiences that delight millions. This innovation is fueled by cutting-edge hardware developed within the Hardware Engineering Group. As a vital part of this organization, the System RF group designs and characterizes wireless systems across Aminutepple’s flagship products—including iPhone, Watch, iPad, Mac, and Audio—ensuring world-class performance from prototype to production. By building these systems, you will empower engineers to arrive at critical decisions with unprecedented speed and accuracy, directly influencing the next generation of Apple innovation.

Masters or PHD in Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Computer Science or a related field.
Expert-level knowledge of multi-agent system design, including sophisticated orchestration, coordination, and persistent state management.
Strong command of Agent Communication Protocols (e.g., MCP, A2A) and frameworks for designing distributed agentic workflows.
Expert-level software development skills with a solid foundation in architectural design principles and the creation of scalable, modular systems.
Proven ability to lead cross-functional architecture discussions and translate ambitious product goals into robust technical system designs.
Preferred qualifications: 10+ years of professional experience in AI/ML-related projects, demonstrating a long-term track record of innovation and technical leadership.
Proven ability to build efficient interfaces for agents to invoke APIs, query high-dimensional databases, and interact with custom toolsets.
Proficiency in Python (Core and Async) and a strong command of FastAPI or Flask for serving high-performance AI endpoints.
Proven success in deploying Generative AI solutions tailored to complex, high-dimensional, and domain-specific engineering data.
Prior experience overseeing the full lifecycle of large-scale software applications deployed within an enterprise-grade production environment.
Deep understanding of model selection, intelligent routing, and fallback strategies to ensure reliability across multiple LLM providers.
Experience developing and implementing rigorous Gen AI evaluation systems to measure the performance, safety, and accuracy of deployed agents.

title: Designer, Design Team
description:
Marcom is the creatively-led global team that oversees Apple's consumer facing marketing. We ensure the flawless development and execution of world-class communications across all medias and platforms. Every day, hundreds of millions of Apple customers around the world interact with our products. We drive the strategy and creative work that provide both new and existing customers with simple, engaging and inspiring marketing experiences.
The Design Team is responsible for the design and art direction of core communications—including product launches and seasonal campaigns—across Retail, Channel, Packaging, Keynote, and Events. Working in a highly collaborative manner, a primary focus of the Design Team is to define the look and feel of all Apple product images and motion through experimentation, critical thinking, and extraordinary attention to detail.
The Designer is an integral member of the team building innovative and compelling work that meets the requirements outlined in creative briefs—from ideation to execution. In this role, you will be instrumental in developing work that inspires both current and potential customers for one of the most beloved brands.

Portfolio exhibiting an understanding of design principles, animation principles, motion theory, typography and visual communication

Excellent skills with design software, primarily the Adobe Creative Suite.
Experience with 3D and motion software, such as Cinema 4D and Adobe After Effects.

title: Display Module Engineer
description:
Apple is looking for a world class module design engineer to lead the design, development and qualification activities of the next generation smart display technology and products.
This individual will serve as a focal point in driving new display technology development and implementation of critical technology platforms to improve display performance, from design conception to hardware and experience prototyping, and to final products. You will be a directly responsible individual to collaborate with multi-functional teams on prototyping efforts for architecture definition, work with suppliers to understand design tolerance and sensitivities, optimize system-level performance based on critical metrics, and validate system designs through engineering builds and design of experiments.
A successful candidate needs to be comfortable with new technology, curiosity and openness to learn new things, a flexible problem solver, meticulous in attention to detail and motivated to drive results. You should be able to tackle problems outside of your respective technical area, have strong presentation and communication skills, and thrive in a hands-on environment that values engineering excellence and innovation. You will be part of something big; come join us!
Minimum qualifications: Bachelors Degree in EE, Optics, Physics, Materials science, or a related field with 10+ years of relevant experience
Experience in one or more of the following : optical design and characterization, optical simulation, physical and geometrical optics, semiconductor optoelectronics, display technologies, sensors, technologies and statistical analysis
Experience leading engineering builds, planning test activities, and managing readiness of module deliverables across development phases
Experience with tools for data acquisition and analysis (Python, LabVIEW), statistical analysis (JMP, MATLAB), and optical simulation (LightTools, FDTD, Zemax, Code V) is strongly desired
Hands-on experience with optical and electrical measurement systems for characterization, testing and validation
Preferred qualifications: MS, or PhD in EE, Optics, Physics, Materials Science, or a related field with 3 years of industry experience
Experience with different display technologies (transmissive, emissive, reflective etc), LED illumination design, fundamental understanding of optics and device physics are a big plus in driving architecture definition and convergence
Experience in module engineering, module integration, or high-volume manufacturing processes. Direct mass-production experience is highly beneficial

title: Engineering Program Manager, SWE Factory
description:
Why Apple? We live in a mobile and device driven world where knowledge of the physical world around us is needed. We rely on this knowledge to get around, to learn about our environment and to enable spectacular new features for custom applications. This is a highly cross functional role and will involve working with our Hardware, Software and Operations teams to track and manage the delivery of Software to the factory lines for the iPhone, iPad, Mac, WATCH, Apple TV and Vision Pro product lines. Knowledge of Software and Hardware product lifecycle
Exceptional verbal and written communication as well as presentation skills
BS/MS EE/CS/CE or relevant experience

Demonstrated creative and critical thinking
Self-motivated and pro-active with demonstrated creative and critical thinking
Experience in consumer electronics factory line

title: Environment, Health and Safety Engineer
description:
In Places, we don’t sit back and let things happen, we make things happen, and we do this in service to all Apple employees and customers. Our team is a diverse and nimble group that manages Apple’s retail stores, workplaces, and workplace services. We develop and manage Apple’s global real estate portfolio, lead all related capital construction projects, provide outstanding facilities and site services, develop and lead sustainability initiatives to reduce the environmental impact of all Apple facilities, including commute and renewable energy programs, and do everything we can to ensure the health and safety of all Apple personnel, facilities, and customers in our facilities around the world.
The Apple Environment, Health & Safety (EHS) team dedicated to protecting the environment, health, and safety of our employees, contractors, customers, and the global communities where we operate. As a team member, you will be instrumental in program implementation, incident review and follow-up, and continuous improvement focused on supporting Corporate operations (research and development, services, projects, maintenance etc.) in Santa Clara Valley (SCV).
We are seeking a skilled and collaborative EHS Operations professional to join our team as an EHS Engineer. The successful candidate will be focused on ensuring business groups receive an extraordinary level of service. They must be passionate about solving problems, possess excellent organizational skills, and communicate effectively across technical disciplines. Additionally, they must have a proven track record of delivering high-quality results on time, taking ownership of issues and tasks with an appropriate sense of urgency, and making hard calls when needed.
The EHS Engineer will provide EHS support to various Corporate team operations and manage regulatory compliance obligations in Apple owned/operated facilities in SCV. They will facilitate safety risk assessments, perform chemical reviews, participate in facility upgrade projects, implement and maintain EHS programs, perform building and lab inspections, conduct accident/incident investigations, provide emergency response, provide operational EHS support of facility/lab construction projects, manage the SCV pesticide program, and manage active air permits including annual updates and air regulation interpretation for compliance. The role will report to the SCV EHS Operations Manager.
Minimum qualifications: At least 7 years of EHS operations experience
BA/BS in environmental engineering, chemical engineering, or an EHS-based degree or equivalent experience
In-depth knowledge of California Air Resources Board (CARB) and Bay Area Air Quality Management District (BAAQMD) rules/regulations.
Air regulation permitting experience and inspection experience.

Research and development lab or semiconductor facility operations experience.

Experience with physical safety, equipment and battery safety, fire safety and emergency response.
Nationally recognized professional credentials (i.e., Board Certified Safety Professional (ASP, CSP), Certified Industrial Hygienist (CIH), Certified Hazardous Materials Manager (CHMM)).
Experience conducting new equipment/new process EHS design review.
Experience working and communicating with all levels of an organization.
Excellent problem-solving, organizational, and reporting skills.

title: Lab Manager
description:
Our team designs, builds, and tests next-generation hardware and technologies that power Apple products used by hundreds of millions of people around the world. We're looking for a Lab Manager to help us maintain a world-class engineering lab environment where our teams can innovate quickly, safely, and reliably.
As Lab Manager, you'll wear two hats: you'll lead and develop a team of lab technicians/coordinators while also rolling up your sleeves as an individual contributor — running experiments, operating equipment, and directly supporting engineering programs. This is a hybrid player-coach role for someone who wants both people leadership and hands-on technical ownership. You'll ensure the lab runs safely and efficiently while also being a technical resource engineers can rely on day-to-day.

3+ years of hands-on experience working in a technical/engineering lab environment, including direct execution of tests and equipment operation

Excellent organizational skills with the ability to balance individual technical work with team management responsibilities

Demonstrated ability to switch fluidly between hands-on technical work and people leadership in a fast-paced environment
Familiarity with EHS regulations (OSHA, EPA) and chemical/electrical safety protocols
Experience with inventory/asset management software and procurement systems
Strong interpersonal and communication skills; ability to work cross-functionally with engineers, technicians, and vendors
Project management experience or certification (PMP, Six Sigma, etc.)
Experience supporting confidential or prototype-stage hardware programs

title: Machine Learning Engineer, Answers Knowledge and Information - Proactive
description:
The Information Intelligence team is creating groundbreaking technology for artificial intelligence, machine learning and natural language processing! The features we create are redefining how hundreds of millions of people use their computers and mobile devices to search and find what they are looking for. Our universal search engine powers search features across a variety of Apple products, including Siri, Spotlight, Safari, Messages and Lookup. We also develop state-of-the-art generative AI technologies based on Large Language Models to power innovative features in both Apple’s devices and services on the cloud. As part of this group, you will be doing large scale machine learning and deep learning research and development to improve Open Domain Question Answering (using both structured knowledge graph data and unstructured web data) and Summarization as well as developing fundamental building blocks needed for Artificial Intelligence. This involves developing sophisticated machine learning and large language models (LLMs) to understand user queries, retrieve and rank relevant documents across multiple sources and synthesize information across documents to provide user with a direct answer that best satisfies their intent and information seeking needs. Additionally, you will research and develop the state-of-the-art LLMs for summarizing personal data such as emails, messages, and notifications. You will also work with researchers and data scientists to develop, fine-tune, and evaluate domain specific Large Language Models for various tasks and applications in Apple’s AI powered products and conduct applied research to transfer the cutting edge research in generative AI to production ready technologies.
As a member of our fast-paced group, you’ll have the unique and rewarding opportunity to shape upcoming products from Apple. We are looking for highly motivated machine learning engineers and researchers having strong machine learning and deep learning fundamentals with hands-on experience in fine-tuning deep learning and large language models.
Minimum qualifications: Experience in modeling user behavior including personalization, online learning and recommendation systems
Experience working with machine learning or LLM model development for various NLP tasks and RAG applications including prompt engineering, training data collection and generation, model fine-tuning and model evaluation
Experience working with Python and at least one of the deep learning frameworks such as TensorFlow, PyTorch, or JAX
Preferred qualifications: PhD in Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, or a related field.
At least 2 years of experience in various state-of-the-art techniques related to LLM fine-tuning in 1 or more of the following areas -- Supervised Fine-tuning (SFT) with Rejection Sampling, Preference-based fine-tuning techniques (e.g RLHF, Reward model, DPO, PPO, GRPO etc.), Parameter efficient fine-tuning techniques (e.g LoRA), Hallucination reduction and factual accuracy improvements, Designing and implementing safety guardrails
Consistent track record of researching, inventing and/or shipping advanced machine learning models
Outstanding communication and interpersonal skills with ability to work with cross-functional teams

title: Manager, Engineering Program Manager, Intelligent System Experience

title: Product RF Design Engineer
description:
You will have a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity to deliver outstanding performance for wireless products. As a member of the Product RF Design team, you will be at the forefront of wireless technology as we push the boundaries of achievable performance in wireless for innovative products. You will become part of a hands-on product development team that develops and influences current and future generations of Apple products.

Product RF Design Engineers should have a broad-based knowledge in RF architecture, design, integration and manufacturing. They have deep theoretical and practical knowledge in one or more areas of electromagnetic theory, RF and Wireless circuit design, communication theory, and product design trade-off. title: RF System Integration Engineer
description:
Do you have a passion for wireless technologies? Do you want to impact the wireless experience for billions of users? Come and join us! You will become part of a hands-on development team that furthers engineering perfection, creativity, and innovation with a prime focus on wireless accuracy and performance. Dynamic, encouraging people and innovative technologies are the norm here. Bring passion and dedication to your job and there's no telling what you could accomplish! As an RF Systems integration engineer, you will be engaged in the design validation for different wireless technologies right from the prototyping phase to mass production. Intuitive understanding in one or all of the following areas: RF Transceiver Blocks, Communications theory, RF Parameters
Familiarity with RF/wireless test equipment and associated RF measurements
Ability to read and write clean, clear, efficient and understandable code in one or more relevant programming languages (C, C++, Python).
International and domestic travel is required (~15%)
Preferred qualifications: MSEE is preferred
5+ Years of industry experience or equivalent. Knowledge of Object Oriented Programming and scalable software design principles
Recent experience in developing test solutions for current and upcoming wireless RF standards (e.g. WiFi 802.11xx, Bluetooth 5.0, 5G, NFC, UWB)
Familiarity with tools that enable high volume manufacturing of these technologies Experience
Ability to break down complex problems and evaluate tradeoffs between proposed solutions
Energy and aim to thrive in a start-up like environment.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills

title: Security Manager, SEAR
description:
Apple engineers have always focused on one person when they build software — the person who will use it. Working in our Software Group (SWE) you’ll see why every Apple product and service feels intuitive and simple, and why every aspect of this group’s work is built around a respect for the customer’s needs.
Apple's Security Engineering & Architecture team (SEAR) focuses on security needs. Passionate about safeguarding, we believe the best defense is a good offense. When it comes to securing more than a billion devices running the world's most sophisticated operating systems, that means finding vulnerabilities first.
We are now making our security evaluation pipeline fully AI-native, from vulnerability discovery to validation, using the most advanced AI capabilities available. Can you make a difference on this scale? Join our extraordinary team of security researchers, engineers and AI specialists, and help discover and patch Apple products' vulnerabilities before they ship.
We are looking for a manager to lead several teams that develop the capabilities and tooling supporting both offensive and defensive security projects. You will bring a product-oriented mindset to complex systems, shaping our end-to-end security evaluation pipeline and driving its evolution toward an AI-native approach.
Your organization will include software and security engineers and AI engineers who bring advanced AI capabilities into every stage of the work. Your teams will partner very closely with Apple's security researchers, who are your primary customers and collaborators. You will make sure they have the tools that make the difference: you will understand their workflows, anticipate their needs, and turn their feedback and ideas into reliable products that multiply their impact. You will set technical direction, grow and mentor your teams, and ensure that what they build is adopted and used across Apple.
Working alongside a wide variety of teams and vendors, your influence will be felt throughout Apple's products, such as iPhone, iPad, Mac and Apple TV. The tools your teams build will support security assessments in the areas of platform security, hardware/software boundary, wireless technologies, and more.
The typical activities of your teams include creating innovative offensive and defensive security tools, building and scaling fuzzing infrastructure and techniques, and developing AI-driven vulnerability discovery and analysis systems. They also include operating research tooling as production services, and consulting with researchers and other teams on both hardware and software, so that proofs of concept, design and specification reviews, and assessments benefit from the best possible tooling. The scope is as diverse as it is essential.
This position requires someone with strong technical skills, the ability to lead and grow multidisciplinary engineering teams, and a customer-focused mindset toward researchers. You should also have a passionate desire to secure systems by enabling the people who show how they can be broken.
If this is you, we'd love to hear from you!
Minimum qualifications: 5+ years of experience managing software development and/or tooling teams
Extraordinary leadership and organizational skills
Strong verbal and written communication skills in English
Preferred qualifications: Knowledge of iOS and macOS security architecture
Familiarity with applied ML and LLM-based agent systems and their evaluation
Familiarity with DevOps practices (CI/CD, containerization/Kubernetes, observability) for scaling internal tooling

title: Senior Data Scientist, Apple Ads
description:
At Apple, we focus deeply on our customers’ experience. Apple Ads brings this same approach to advertising, helping people find exactly what they’re looking for and helping advertisers grow their businesses.
Our technology powers ads and sponsorships across Apple Services, including the App Store, Apple News, and MLS Season Pass. Everything we do is designed for trust, connection, and impact: We respect user privacy, integrate advertising thoughtfully into the experience, and deliver value for advertisers of all sizes, from small app developers to global brands. Because when advertising is done right, it benefits everyone.
The Data Insights organization helps Apple Ads understand, measure, forecast, optimize, and improve the advertising ecosystem across Apple Services. We partner closely with Product, Engineering, Finance, Sales, and Leadership teams to solve complex business and product challenges using data, experimentation, statistical modeling, and machine learning.
We are hiring Data Scientists across multiple teams and areas of focus within Apple Ads. Successful candidates may be considered for a variety of opportunities depending on their experience, interests, and technical strengths. Our hiring process is designed to match candidates to the teams and problem spaces where they can have the greatest impact.
As a Data Scientist within Data Insights, you will work on high-impact problems that influence product strategy, business performance, advertiser outcomes, and marketplace health across Apple's advertising platforms. Depending on your area of focus, you may contribute to one or more of the following domains:
- Product and Marketplace Insights: Define measurement frameworks, design experiments, evaluate product and advertiser outcomes, and identify marketplace opportunities that influence product strategy and decision-making.
- Business Insights: Own key business metrics, identify drivers of business performance, and translate analytical findings into actionable recommendations for leadership. Build scalable analytical frameworks and automation solutions that improve decision-making across the advertising ecosystem.
- Predictive Modeling, Forecasting & Optimization: Develop forecasting, machine learning, and optimization models that improve business performance and operational decision-making. Design robust evaluation frameworks and translate model outputs into scalable business impact.

Deep familiarity with experiment design and quasi-experimental frameworks

Experience working on real-time bidding systems, advertising technology platforms, or attribution methodologies

title: Senior Firmware Engineer

title: Senior Software Engineer - Tools, Intelligent Automation & Developer Platforms
description:

title: Market Analyst
description:
ABOUT BASE

Base is America’s next-generation power company. We’re rebuilding the foundation of modern civilization–electricity–by deploying a vast network of distributed batteries that is transforming today’s fragile, centralized grid into a resilient and abundant system. We are engineers, operators, and creatives solving some of the most complex, interdisciplinary challenges of our time.




ABOUT THE ROLE

Base’s Risk & Trading team turns a fleet of distributed batteries and the households we serve into a power business that makes money. As a Market Analyst, you’ll know how much Base is earning, where it could lose money, and how it will make money in the next market.

You’ll own P&L (profit and loss) reporting and risk tracking across our battery fleet and retail operations. You’ll build the pricing models behind what we charge members, recommend hedges, and work with Finance, Growth and Legal & Policy to figure out how Base makes money in each new market. Base already does this in ERCOT. Your first job is to do it in PJM.

This role suits someone with a few years of experience in power markets, retail energy, or a related analytical field. You’ll own real decisions early.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Build a bottoms-up retail pricing model for PJM that builds upon our ERCOT model.

 - Bring PJM into our risk system and P&L reporting, so we know the margin we earn and how to buy supply.

 - Identify new market opportunities and work closely with stakeholders from Finance, Growth and Legal & Policy teams to bring them to reality.

 - Recommend changes to Base’s hedging strategy in ERCOT and PJM, and track our exposure against risk limits.




WHAT YOU’LL BRING

 - Energy markets knowledge: you understand wholesale market basics in ERCOT and PJM, including how power is bought, hedged and settled. You know how retail pricing and operations work.

 - Commercial sense: you understand how a retail offer makes or loses money. You can explain the cost to supply it, the margin on it, and the risk in between.

 - Risk and statistics: you think in distributions, not point forecasts. You know power prices are tail heavy. Basic statistics is enough.

 - Coding and SQL: you build reports and models in Python (or another language), pull your own data with SQL, and work through a problem independently.

Nice to have: experience at a retail energy provider, utility supply desk, or trading middle office.



ABOUT THE TEAM

Base’s Risk & Trading team turns the grid-service capability of our distributed battery fleet into revenue. That means building and defending the models that decide which markets and products Base participates in, from real-time arbitrage to multi-year distribution deals. The team’s calls carry real weight - a mis-modeled coincident peak or an unvetted market opinion shows up directly in Base’s book. You’ll work alongside traders, market operations engineers, and policy leads who bring the same rigor to distribution-scale energy that a trading desk brings to wholesale power.



Please note: Base is a startup, which means priorities shift and evolve quickly. Your role may expand or change based on the needs of the business at any given time, so the responsibilities listed may not be exhaustive.




OUR VALUES

 - First Principles Thinking: Question assumptions. Principles > rules.

 - Operate at Base Pace: Focus on what matters, act quickly, and learn by doing.

 - Give & Get Feedback: Be direct, be humble, and maintain a growth mindset.

 - Everyone’s an Owner: Follow through on commitments and own results.

 - Strong Opinions, Loosely Held: Drive clarity and make calls with imperfect information.

 - Committed to the Mission: Rebuilding the grid is a big challenge. We work hard because we care deeply about the impact we’re creating. We work in-person. It’s not a 9-to-5. We are all-in.

 - Fun & Optimism Coexist with Grit: Collaboration and celebration coincide with the intensity of building real things.
   
   


DO THE BEST WORK OF YOUR LIFE AT BASE.

As a frontline operator, you will serve as the first line of defense during emerging incidents—monitoring systems, assessing risk, executing SOPs, and escalating issues quickly and accurately. In addition to core operational response, you will apply foundational analytical skills to validate information, distinguish signal from noise, provide clear operational context that supports timely escalation and informed decision-making. Ensure Seamless Shift Handover: Produce concise shift reports and conduct disciplined handovers that capture incident status, risk context, and outstanding actions.
Contribute to Operational Excellence: Participate in drills, retrospectives, and continuous improvement efforts to strengthen GOC readiness, workflows, and analytical rigor.
Operate Calmly Under Pressure: Demonstrate professionalism, composure, and sound judgment during fast-moving or high-impact incidents.

title: Engineering Manager, Personalization
description:
About the Team
DoorDash is looking for an Engineering Manager with an ML background to lead the Personalization engineering team. This team is responsible for building ML ranking and recommendation systems to maximize the value for consumers, merchants, and DoorDash.
Our Personalization team is a part of our Core Consumer org which owns the top of the conversion funnel from the initial landing page all the way to checkout across platforms. Personalization is at the center of the team’s mission. As DoorDash expands into new verticals and experiences like grocery, reservations, and going out, the challenge of helping consumers easily find what they want grows exponentially, so the opportunity is massive!
In 2027, we’re reimagining personalization from the ground up: an intent agent that predicts, at app open, what each consumer is here for; semantic understanding of every entity we rank; a blender that blends content from different verticals and business lines, like reservations, going out, and ads; and real-time ranking that adapts as consumer signals happen.
About the Role
You will lead a team of world-class ML engineers redefining the personalization experience for DoorDash through cutting-edge technologies. You will also be the key player in defining DoorDash’s personalization strategy and technology roadmap.
You’re excited about this opportunity because you will…
Build an intent agent that makes granular predictions of what each consumer is here for the moment they open the app, and shapes the experience around it
Leverage cutting-edge LLM and Deep Learning (GNN, MTL, Transformers) to augment DoorDash’s personalization stack, starting with semantic understanding of every entity we rank, so our models understand what consumers want and what we offer, not just what they clicked before
Extend the blender to blend content from different verticals and business lines, like reservations, going out, and ads, balancing value for consumers, merchants, and DoorDash
Take personalization to real-time ranking that reacts to consumer signals as they happen
Lead and grow a team of exceptional machine learning engineers delivering on end-to-end personalization experience with state-of-the-art ML approaches
Work with Product, Design, and Business stakeholders directly across DoorDash to define the roadmap and vision for the team and deliver immense impact
Encourage innovation, implementation of cutting-edge technologies, outside-of-the-box thinking and teamwork
Build an outstanding team by coaching and empowering engineers through delegation, and applying your technical expertise to hold your team to the highest engineering standards
Scale the team by developing internal talent and attracting top external talent
We're excited about you because you have…
B.S., M.S., or PhD. in Computer Science or equivalent
7+ years of industry experience
Minimum of 2 years of leadership experience
Broad knowledge of machine learning with strong ML modeling foundation
Extensive experience in building user-facing product and working directly with product managers
Strong communication skills and the ability to partner with teams spanning many disciplines
Ability to guide and grow an excellent engineering team in a rapidly changing business environment
Nice to have
Experience leading the successful application of machine learning to real-world ranking and recommendation problems
Experience with LLM-powered agents, semantic representations of users and content, multi-objective blending, or real-time ML systems

title: Senior Manager, Protective Services
description:
About the Team
DoorDash is one of the world's most trusted on-demand logistics platforms. The Global Safety and Security team exists to keep it that way, protecting our people, property, operations, brand, and reputation across all our markets. We manage risk and create value through agility, technology, and a people-first approach. Our DoorDash, Deliveroo, and Wolt brands now span more than 40 countries, dozens of offices, and tens of thousands of employees. Protective Services is the function accountable for the safety of the people we protect and the environments they live and work in, wherever they are.
About the Role
We are hiring a Senior Manager, Protective Services to lead protective operations, reporting to the Director, Protective Services. This is as much a build-and-execute mandate as a leadership one. You own the decisions that keep protection working, including how teams are staffed and assigned, how protection is set for a given person and situation, what we spend and which vendors we use, what people are trained to do, and how incidents get handled.
This is a player-coach role, and the coaching half does not keep you off the field. You will work advances, travel with the people we protect, and take your turn in the rotation while setting the standard the team works to. Protection here is a service. It works when the people we protect can move through their lives with as little friction as we can manage, and when they trust the team enough to tell us what we need to know.
You own protective operations, training and standards, vendor management, incident response, and converged physical-cyber protection. Protective teams, intelligence, and cybersecurity work on the same problem simultaneously, and detection and intelligence capabilities drive our protective posture.
Success in the first year means a tight operating rhythm, training and qualification standards that hold up against the best protective programs, a team that is current and deployable on short notice, and protective decisions driven by intelligence rather than reaction.
You are excited about this opportunity because you will…
Lead protective operations. Own staffing, assignment, protective decisions, resourcing, and response across the full scope of the program. Lead from within the work rather than from above it, and be accountable for how it performs.
Own training and standards. Set what people are trained on, qualified in, and expected to keep current, then verify it is happening and hold the records that prove it. Build a team that deploys on short notice and stays that way.
Own vendor and supplier management. Decide what we need and from whom, run competitive procurement, and set approval thresholds. Where a supplier is part of how we protect someone, they meet our standard.
Own incident response. Be the escalation point for protective events within your authority and make real-time calls on protection and resourcing. Escalate immediately on legal exposure, law enforcement involvement, or risk that reaches other teams, and write down what was decided and why.
Lead converged physical-cyber protection. Work with Protective Intelligence and Cyber Protective Services to read threat indicators and judge what testing and assessment findings actually mean. When a threat starts online, you decide how protection answers it.
Earn trust and keep friction low. Build relationships with the people we protect, their families, and their teams to make protection something they rely on rather than tolerate. Design the friction out, so we ask less of them for the same result.
We are excited about you because you bring…
Leadership and operating experience. Ten or more years in protective, security, or military operations, including five or more years managing people with hands-on responsibility for protective operations. You have held real decision authority, not advised someone who held it, and you are still close enough to the work to run it yourself.
Judgment under pressure. You make sound calls with incomplete information in fast-moving, high-consequence situations, and the record of those decisions holds up under later review.
Building, not inheriting. A track record of building or scaling protective capability and setting the standards, qualifications, and procedures other leads work to.
Breadth of scope. Experience running more than one protective discipline or program at the same time, including through other leads, accountable for cost, method, and staffing across all of it.
Technical fluency across physical and cyber security. You do not need to be a security engineer, but you need to think like one. You understand how networked systems are put together and how someone would go about taking them apart, you are comfortable with network security concepts, access control, surveillance, and residential security technology at the operational level, and you can tell whether a proposed fix actually closes the gap it claims to.
Service orientation and discretion. You have earned the confidence of the people you protect and the people close to them, and you have kept it. You handle sensitive information about who is protected, how, and where without exception.
Working well across teams. A record of partnering with intelligence, cybersecurity, legal, and business teams on matters that go beyond your authority.
Availability. Willingness to travel around 35 percent, with peaks near 50 percent, often on short notice, and to pick up the phone on protective events and serious escalations outside working hours.
Physical readiness for the work. The ability to stay on your feet and moving for long stretches across offices, residences, venues, and transit, to lift and carry equipment up to 50 pounds, to assist or move a person to safety, to work in tight spaces and sit in vehicles and aircraft for extended periods, to see and assess people, vehicles, and conditions at distance and in poor light, to communicate clearly in loud environments, and to drive in heavy traffic and bad conditions.
Endurance for the conditions. The ability to work outdoors and in transit in extreme heat, extreme cold, inclement weather, and crowds for as long as the work takes, to work irregular and long hours including nights, weekends, and holidays on short or broken sleep and across time zones, and to keep making good decisions while doing it.
Education. Bachelor's degree or equivalent professional experience.
We expect this position to be filled by 10/13/2026.
