title: Senior Data Engineer
description:
About MISUMI Americas
MISUMI Americas, a division of MISUMI Group, is a leading provider of standard, configurable, and custom manufacturing solutions. By integrating a vast catalog of components with a world-class digital manufacturing platform, MISUMI Americas empowers engineers and procurement teams to accelerate innovation across the entire product lifecycle. With operations in the San Francisco Bay Area and Chicago, the company serves as a vital partner for the most innovative companies in the Americas.
Senior Data Engineer - Schaumburg
MISUMI | Data Platform
Own the data platform that MISUMI runs on
MISUMI is looking for a Senior Data Engineer to be the go-to owner of our Snowflake warehouse, dbt project, and data pipelines. You will be the primary data engineer, with real ownership and real influence: the models you build and the pipelines you run are what Operations, Finance, Sales, Marketing, Engineering, Product, and Customer Support rely on to make decisions every day.
You will work hands-on with a modern stack (Snowflake, dbt, Fivetran, Git/GitHub) and with AI coding agents in your daily engineering work. You will also have the autonomy to take requests from intake to production, propose what we should build next, and shape safe team practices for agentic development. If you want a role where your judgment directly determines whether the business can trust its data, this is it.
Impact in this Role
The Senior Data Engineer is the go-to owner of MISUMI’s Snowflake warehouse, dbt project, and data pipelines. This person turns data from business and production systems into trusted, analytics-ready models that Operations, Finance, Sales, Marketing, Engineering, Product, and Customer Support use to make decisions. Because this is the primary data engineering role, the accuracy, security, and reliability of the data platform, including regulated data such as CUI, depend on this person’s judgment and execution.
Essential Functions
Administer Snowflake: manage users, roles, grants, warehouses, resource monitors and security policies, and keep the environment secure, fast and cost-efficient.
Design, build, and own dbt models (staging, intermediate, marts, and the semantic layer) that turn replicated source data into trusted, analytics-ready tables with tests and documentation.
Build, operate, and monitor ELT pipelines from production and business systems into Snowflake, using Fivetran and related tools. Resolve connector failures, schema changes, backfills, and data-quality issues.
Act as the team’s primary technical resource for modeling and pipeline work. Take requests from intake to production independently, including scoping, estimating, and reporting status.
Translate business requirements into technical requirements and data models, and bridge the gap between business teams and technology. Ask clarifying questions, agree on metric definitions and acceptance criteria with stakeholders, and turn them into specifications the team can build and test.
Proactively identify opportunities where data, modeling, or automation can help the business get closer to its goals, and propose and prioritize them with stakeholders instead of waiting for requests.
Run an impact analysis before changing, deprecating, or removing any shared table, model, or connector. Use dbt lineage, Snowflake dependency and access metadata, and stakeholder review, and document a rollback plan.
Own the Git and GitHub workflow for the dbt project: branching standards, pull-request review, automated tests, and deployment.
Use AI assistants and agentic workflows in daily engineering work to speed up SQL and dbt development, testing, documentation, code review, and debugging, and help set safe team practices for using them.
Find the root cause of data-quality, performance, and pipeline problems and fix them at the source.
Tune queries, models, and warehouse usage, and advise engineers and analysts on efficient query patterns and table design.
Maintain data dictionaries, data-flow diagrams, and schema documentation.
Lead data design sessions and technical reviews, and explain design trade-offs to technical and non-technical stakeholders.
Evaluate new Snowflake and dbt features and tools, and recommend improvements to the data platform.
Mentor analysts and engineers on SQL and dbt best practices.
Work with remote, cross-functional teams across time zones.
Maintain and contribute to the Quality Management System (QMS).
Desired Traits
Five core skills. Candidates must show direct, hands-on production experience in each:
Snowflake administration and engineering: access control, warehouse sizing and cost control, query tuning, clustering, security controls, cloning, time travel, and data sharing.
dbt expert modeling: layered models, dimensional modeling, incremental models, snapshots, macros, tests, documentation, and CI/CD through Git.
Advanced SQL: CTEs, window functions, recursive queries, semi-structured data, and query tuning.
ETL/ELT tooling: Fivetran (our tool) or similar, including connector setup, schema drift, deleted records, backfills, and cost.
Agentic coding and development: daily use of AI coding agents that work in the repository and terminal (not chat-only use), with disciplined verification of everything they produce.
Required
Bachelor’s degree in Data Science, Computer Science, Information Systems, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
10+ years of experience as a data engineer, designing, building, and operating data pipelines and warehouses.
6+ years of hands-on Snowflake experience in production, including administration: access control, warehouse management, and cost and performance monitoring.
5+ years building and maintaining production dbt projects (dbt Core or dbt Cloud), including testing, documentation, incremental models, macros, and CI/CD.
5+ years working with ETL/ELT tools such as Fivetran, Airbyte, Stitch, Matillion, Informatica, or Talend, plus experience with pipeline orchestration.
Demonstrated, hands-on experience using agentic coding tools that work directly in the codebase (not chat-only AI use) in daily data engineering work. This includes building agentic workflows or tool integrations for data work, such as MCP servers, custom agents, or automated dbt and pipeline checks, with concrete examples of the workflows and results.
Expert SQL, including CTEs, window functions, and performance tuning.
Daily use of Git and GitHub pull-request workflows.
Experience being the primary or sole owner of a data platform, or the technical lead for one.
Experience administering data platforms that hold regulated data (such as CUI under NIST SP 800-171), including access control, audit logging, encryption, and data classification. Must be able to pass a background check and complete required CUI and security training.
Preferred
Direct Fivetran experience, including connector management.
Experience with Sigma Computing, or with Tableau, Looker, or a similar BI tool.
Experience modeling ERP and CRM data, such as NetSuite or Salesforce.
Python for data tooling and automation.
Snowflake SnowPro certification or dbt certification.
Infrastructure-as-code experience for Snowflake, such as Terraform.
Background in manufacturing, supply chain, or marketplace businesses.
Abilities
Write advanced SQL on large, complex datasets, including semi-structured data such as JSON in Snowflake VARIANT columns.
Apply data warehousing and dimensional modeling principles to turn business requirements into well-structured, maintainable models.
Work independently: take an open-ended problem, define the approach, deliver it, and raise risks early instead of stalling.
Use sound production judgment: verify before changing shared systems, plan for failure, and know how to roll back.
Use AI tools with discipline: give clear context and constraints, review and test every AI-generated change, and stay accountable for the result.
Solve hard problems methodically: break an unclear problem into testable hypotheses, gather evidence from logs, lineage, and query history, confirm the cause before changing anything, and verify the fix worked.
Communicate clearly in writing and in person, giving business context to engineers and technical context to non-engineers.
Physical Demands
The employee routinely sits, talks, hears, and uses hands and fingers to operate a keyboard. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
Travel
Ability to travel 5% annually in the US for team meetings, offsites, and conferences.
Ready to own the platform?
If you have run production Snowflake, dbt, and ELT at scale, you work daily with agentic coding tools, and you want to be the person the business trusts with its data, we would like to hear from you. Apply today.
Salary range:
$167,000 - $202,300 base salary per year, depending on experience
Benefits include, but are not limited to:
Comprehensive medical and dental coverage
401(k) plan
Generous PTO and leave programs
We’re actively seeking teammates who:
Bring diverse perspectives and experience to our culture and company.
Excel at being part of a strong, empathetic team.
Thrive in an environment emphasizing respect, honesty, collaboration, and growth.
Have an ‘always learning’ mindset that celebrates learning, not just wins.
Help us continue to build a world-class organization that values the contributions of all of our teammates
We encourage applications from members of underrepresented groups, including but not limited to women, members of the LGBTQ community, people of color, people with disabilities, and veterans.

title: Senior Electro Mechanical Design Engineer - Plant
description:
Are you ready to build America’s energy future? Form Energy is an American manufacturing and energy technology company. We’re revolutionizing energy storage with cost-effective, multi-day technology designed to keep the electric grid secure and reliable, even during extended periods of stress. By strengthening the electric system and reimagining what’s possible, we’re giving clean energy a whole new form! 



In recent years, Form Energy has earned a number of accolades, including being named by TIME as a “Best Invention”, MIT Technology Review as a “Top Climate Tech Company To Watch”, and Fast Company as “One of the Next Big Things In Tech”. We are making rapid progress on our mission of delivering energy storage for a better world, and our team is growing just as rapidly to meet demand. We have signed contracts with leading electric utilities across the United States and production of our iron-air batteries is underway at our first high-volume manufacturing facility in West Virginia. 



Working for Form Energy is more than just a job, it’s a chance to be part of something extraordinary. And now - right as we significantly scale up battery manufacturing -  might be the most exciting moment in the company’s history to join. We are assembling a team of highly talented and driven individuals across the country. Driven by our core values of humanity, excellence, and creativity, our team is determined to deliver on our mission and transform the energy landscape for the better.



Feeling energized to make a meaningful impact on the world? Then keep reading - you’ve come to the right place.




ROLE DESCRIPTION

Form Energy is hiring a Senior Electro Mechanical Design Engineer - Plant to optimize the design and manufacturability for our balance of plant equipment. You will produce complex schematics, 3D models, and detailed mechanical prints with all specifications and callouts for a product that can survive and thrive. Your designs will be mindful of all requirements in play including, but not limited to shipping, installation, operational lifetime, and service at our project sites. Moreover, you will specify testing requirements that will prove the functionality and reliability of your designs. Alongside our world-class supply chain team, you will own component selection for your designs and spearhead vendor relationships - from exploring new strategic partnerships to owning releases and engineering changes in our product lifecycle management system. This role will showcase your ability to independently generate and organize engineering documentation and requirements needed to interface with our Electronics, Software, and Project Engineering teams. This is an exciting opportunity to move some serious power at a company focused on creating a reliable and fully renewable electric grid year-round!



Relocation assistance is available. 




WHAT YOU'LL DO:

 - Architecture & Requirements: Identify electrical requirements and define system interfaces for key power conversion equipment, plant, and auxiliary systems.

 - Electrical Design: Author comprehensive electrical schematics for equipment for audiences involved in build, test, installation and service.

 - Component Engineering & Sourcing: Select off-the-shelf (OTS) electromechanical components that comply with relevant safety standards and partner with both external and internal supply chain teams to drive down component pricing and long-lead times.

 - Cabinet Packaging & 3D Layout: Design component  layouts using SolidWorks and/or Eplan to optimize space, cable routing, thermal management, and internal electronics placement.

 - Technical Documentation: Generate manufacturing documentation—including multiline diagrams, component layouts, harness drawings, and Interface Control Documents (ICDs)—for contract manufacturers and internal stakeholders.

 - Testing & Verification Standards: Author functional, performance, and End-of-Line (EOL) test plans and operating procedures to ensure manufacturing quality and field reliability.

 - Prototype Testing & Validation: Perform hands-on validation and characterization for prototypes and vendor first-articles in close coordination with software and project engineering.

 - Reliability & Life-Testing: Work with our reliability team to develop environmental and electrical stress tests to quantify system design life.

 - PLM & Configuration Management: Manage product configuration, engineering releases, and Bills of Materials (BOMs) using SolidWorks PDM and Arena PLM.

 - Field Deployment & Commissioning: Scale lab insights to real-world applications through direct involvement in commissioning and testing first-in-kind field installations.

 - Cross-Functional Support: Support all stages of the power conversion system lifecycle, adapting to evolving product and team needs.




WHAT YOU'LL BRING:

 - Bachelor’s Degree in Electrical or Mechanical Engineering with 4+ years industry experience in electromechanical design.

 - Strong understanding of circuit fundamentals, and the relevant thermal and mechanical considerations  of circuits at high power density and high voltage.

 - Proficiency in electrical design using software packages such as Altium, Eplan, and/or Solidworks Electrical.

 - Experience using CAD software (SolidWorks and/or Eplan) for 3D modeling, component layouts, and product packaging.

 - Hands-on experience assembling, troubleshooting, and validating self-designed equipment and prototypes.

 - Demonstrated experience  designing service procedures and engineering safeguards for high-voltage (1500 VDC) and high-current (> 2 kA) systems; experience applying UL 1741, UL 508A, NFPA 70 and NFPA 70E.

 - Excellent communication skills, with the ability to clearly and succinctly explain design decisions and execute multidisciplinary work.

 - Sense of urgency and self-driven to hit difficult schedule targets.
   



#LI-Onsite

title: Electromechanical Technician
description:
Job Description:
SUMMARY
Performs all related duties necessary for maintenance and repair of machinery and equipment used in production plant; for maintenance and repair of the physical structure, electrical, and plumbing systems of the buildings; and, when necessary, performs various construction/remodeling duties to company property as assigned.  Also performs electrical maintenance and repairs of plant production equipment and commercial building.
ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
Follows all company safety rules and policies.
Must be able to maintain 5S program standards including organizing, labeling, cleaning and sustaining of workstations, toolboxes, work areas and parts shelving and cabinets.
Must be able to read, understands and follows schematics, wire and parts diagrams, sketches, operation manuals and manufacturer’s specifications to repair and maintain machinery and mechanical equipment such as, but not limited to, motors, pneumatic, hydraulic, conveyor systems and production machines and equipment using hand tools, power tools and precision measuring and testing instruments.
Observes mechanical devices in operation and listens to their sounds to locate causes of trouble. Root Cause
Dismantles machines or equipment to gain access to and remove defective parts, replaces defective parts and motors, and adjusts feed mechanisms.  Replaces or repairs machine belts.  Performs these duties with the aid of such equipment as hoists, cranes, hand tools and power tools.
Holds scaffolding members in place or tightens bolts to erect working platforms about machines.
Cleans and lubricates machine parts, such as, but not limited to, shafts, pulleys, gears, and bearings, using rags, brushes, grease gun, oil can, and other required tools not specifically listed here.
Removes dust, dirt, grease and waste material from machines.
Painting machines or equipment to prevent corrosion.
May install and repair electrical systems and electrical and electronic components of industrial machinery and equipment, following electrical code, manuals, schematic diagrams, blueprints and other specifications, using hand tools, power tools and electrical and electronic test equipment.
Observes functioning of installed equipment or system to detect hazards and need for adjustments, relocation or replacement.
May diagnose/troubleshoot malfunctioning equipment, such as control circuits, motors and lighting fixtures, HVAC systems, using testing equipment, and make necessary repairs, such as replacing damaged or broken wires and cables. Troubleshoot to component levels
Tests malfunctioning machinery, using test equipment and discusses malfunction with other maintenance employees to diagnose malfunction.  Replaces faulty electrical components of machinery, such as wiring, fuses, relays, switches, electric motor bearings and motors and positions sensing devices.
May diagnose and repair or replace faulty electronic components, such as circuit boards, and mechanical, hydraulic and pneumatic components of machines and equipment.
Maintains tools and equipment and keeps supplies and parts in order.
May repair electronic equipment such as industrial controls, audio systems, transmitters, and servomechanisms, following blueprints and manufacturers’ specifications and using hand tools and test instruments.
Converses with machinery/equipment operators to ascertain problems with machinery/equipment before breakdown and to determine if breakdown is due to human error or mechanical/electrical problems.
Tests faulty machinery/equipment and applies knowledge of functional operation of electronic/electrical systems or units to diagnose cause of malfunction.
Tests electronic components and circuits to locate defects, using oscilloscopes, signal generators, ammeters and voltmeters. Replaces defective components and wiring and adjusts mechanical parts, using hand tools and soldering iron.  Aligns, adjusts and calibrates equipment according to specifications.
Maintains records of repairs, calibrations and tests.
May connect wiring to lighting fixtures and power equipment, using hand tools.  May install control and distribution components such as switches, relays and circuit-breaker panels, fastening in place with screws or bolts, using hand tools and power tools.
May connect power cables to equipment and installs grounding leads.
Tests continuity of circuit to ensure electrical compatibility and safety of components using testing instruments, such as ohmmeter, battery and buzzer and oscilloscope.
May bend and cut conduit and wire, and drill holes in walls, floors and ceilings for electrical connections.
May connect wire to motors, fixtures, and other electrical equipment, replace switches and fuses and splice wire and insulates wire with friction tape.
May bend, cut and thread pipe, cut openings in walls, ceilings and floors for pipes, seal pipe joints with sealing compound.
May cut out and join parts for worktables, benches, shelves and other furnishings, using power tools and hand tools.
May be required to assist with plumbing repair work, building construction/remodeling/repairs, general machinery maintenance or repair duties.
May patch or replace plaster or plaster board and paint walls, ceilings, and trim of building.
May drill and break up concrete.
May mix and pour concrete for foundations.
May weld and fabricate a variety of deigns, including fixtures, carts, tables, and platforms using MIG, TIG and/or stick methods.
Clears clogged drains and replaces plumbing fixtures.
Inspects products and processes while performing job duties to ensure all work done meets or exceeds standards of the company’s quality program.
Works cooperatively and congenially with co-workers to achieve cohesive and productive work processes and work environment.
May provide ground watch for other maintenance employees using aerial equipment
May be required to assist with spill response clean-up
May be required to train other maintenance employees
Performs additional tasks as assigned by management or as the situation requires.
QUALIFICATIONS
Valid Texas Driver’s License required
3 + years’ experience in general mechanical maintenance of production machinery to include reading blueprints, wire diagrams, pneumatics, hydraulics, welding, root cause analysis, and requesting machine parts.
Possess minimum knowledge of electrical wiring repairs and installation, AC/DC controls, blueprints, schematic diagrams, pneumatics, and hydraulics.
Technical degree and/or license relating to electrical, mechanical or HVAC/Refrigeration - minimum of one preferred OR 40 hours of documented electrical training. License number and/or documentation must be provided before hire date.

Capable of operating aerial lift equipment

description:
Job Description:
Smart People. Smart Ideas. Smart Choice.
Hands-On Field Service Role
MTS is a leading global supplier of test and simulation systems. Formula 1 teams, leading automotive and aerospace companies, and the world's top researchers in materials and seismic engineering all rely on our systems to determine product reliability and ensure compliance with quality standards. Check out some of our amazing technology here: http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vXOsvWpTHH4
What This Role Looks Like
This is a unique, HQ-based Field Service Engineer role for someone who thrives on variety over a fixed territory. As our floater FSE based in Eden Prairie, MN, you'll step into a trainer's or mentor's territory anywhere in North America for the full duration of each training or mentoring event, keeping coverage seamless while they're out. When no event is active, you'll cover PTO, illness, and peak overflow. Being based at MTS headquarters means faster ramp-up, direct access to SMEs and training resources, and central dispatch to wherever coverage is needed next.
Day to day, the work is hands-on: installing, maintaining, calibrating, and troubleshooting complex servo-hydraulic and electro-mechanical test systems at customer sites. Training on MTS-specific technology is provided, and strong hands-on technical aptitude is essential.
Travel: This role involves frequent travel from home base in Eden Prairie, MN to customer sites across North America, since coverage assignments follow wherever a training or mentoring event or overflow need arises. Travel will vary week to week rather than following a fixed regional pattern, and candidates should be genuinely comfortable with, and energized by, a highly travel-oriented role.

Install, maintain, calibrate, and repair computer-controlled servo-hydraulic and electro-mechanical test systems
Diagnosing issues across controllers, hydraulics, data acquisition systems, sensors, transducers, fixtures, and grips
Troubleshoot mechanical, electrical, and control-system issues using hands-on diagnostic methods

Comfort owning customer relationships and troubleshooting complex systems with minimal supervision

Strong communication skills and professional interaction with customers

Industry leading 401(k) plan

Primary Function of Position
This entry level manufacturing engineer will support multiple manufacturing lines for both mature and new instruments and accessories for the Ion platform.  This engineer must be able to support existing manufacturing lines, recommend and implement improved manufacturing processes, and lead manufacturing line transfers.  The role requires the ability to collaborate effectively across functions ranging from Quality and Design to Manufacturing in the US and Mexico.
Essential Job Duties
Lead manufacturing line transfer projects, including: Lead project management effectively, including monitoring schedules for multiple functions across two plants
Procure, assemble, and qualify custom mechanical and electromechanical equipment
Improve equipment documentation and design as needed for continuous improvement in preparation for further transfers
Develop an in-depth understanding of our manufacturing processes, and transfer knowledge to new engineers and assemblers from a remote location to facilitate an effective transfer
Troubleshoot electromechanical equipment problems, including collaboration with third party equipment makers as needed, e.g. braiders, laminators, or testing equipment
Support several Ion manufacturing lines including: Establish regular communication with the production team to ensure they have the best support possible for both short and long term needs
Manage product reliability improvements from concept to implementation
Identify, design, qualify, document and introduce assembly/test fixtures and equipment
Improve process flows of Ion instrument manufacturing lines to optimize for reliability, efficiency, capacity, cost, and technician safety
Execute and mentor others in manufacturing process validations, process FMEAs, and other elements associated with production Master Validation Plans
Provide product and process Design for Manufacturing/Assembly (DFX) input to enhance manufacturability, and lead improvement implementations
Manage manufacturing strategy and production capability for Ion Instrument lines to minimize customer backorders
Maintain compliance with medical device quality system including corrective action closure, discrepant material disposition and Engineering Change Order (ECO) implementation
Provide technical support for failure analyses and root cause investigations of product failures
Contribute to the establishment of group and individual objectives consistent with overall product development goals, including priority setting, establishment of metrics, and effectively communicating progress
Provide resource budget estimates for product and process improvements, tooling development, and testing
Works with Quality and Regulatory to ensure that the team follows appropriate GMP, design history file (DHF), and device history record (DHR) guidelines per FDA requirements

Strong technical problem solving and analytical skills
Familiar with various component manufacturing processes (machining , injection molding & MIM, stamping, coining, extrusion)

Strong organizational skills and ability to work on several fast-paced projects simultaneously
Mechanical design and analysis skills, including statics, dynamics, kinematics, strength of materials, and stress analysis is a plus
Able to communicate effectively and professionally with cross-functional peers, executive leadership, internal customers, and external suppliers
Prior experience with Design Control processes for medical devices and/or clinical applications of the surgical instruments, and/or automated equipment design is a plus
25% travel (including international) is required

B.S. degree in engineering discipline, M.S. preferred

This role combines hands-on technical leadership in SAP ME (Manufacturing Execution) and SAP MII (Manufacturing Integration and Intelligence) with responsibility for leading a team of developers, setting technical direction, and ensuring solutions are scalable, reliable, and aligned with business needs. The ideal candidate is a deeply experienced SAP ME/MII practitioner who can also mentor junior developers, drive best practices, and partner with cross-functional stakeholders to optimize manufacturing processes and real-time data integration.
Key Responsibilities
Lead the design, development, and implementation of SAP ME and SAP MII solutions that integrate manufacturing systems with enterprise SAP applications.
Serve as the technical lead for the ME/MII development team, providing architectural direction, code reviews, and hands-on guidance on complex development efforts.
Mentor and coach junior and mid-level developers, fostering skill growth, knowledge sharing, and adherence to development standards and best practices.
Collaborate with business analysts, functional consultants, plant operations, and IT teams to gather requirements and translate them into robust technical designs.
Design and extend SAP ME applications using the SAP ME SDK, including custom PODs, operations, business logic services, and workflow customizations.

Document solutions, architecture decisions, and configurations for internal knowledge sharing and long-term maintainability.
Drive continuous improvement and optimization of existing applications, tools, and development processes.
Provide training and knowledge transfer to end-users, junior developers, and other team members.

8+ years of experience in SAP ME and/or SAP MII development, including experience leading or mentoring other developers.

Strong experience with SAP MII, including hands-on work with SAP MII 15.x or higher versions.
Experience with SAP HANA and strong understanding of manufacturing execution and shop-floor processes.
Hands-on experience with the UI5 framework to build web applications.
Proven experience integrating SAP ME/MII with other systems such as MES, SCADA, PLCs, and other manufacturing software.
Strong knowledge of Java, XML, JavaScript, and related web technologies.
Experience with SAP PI/PO, SAP ABAP, or other integration technologies.
Demonstrated experience leading technical teams, projects, or workstreams, with the ability to guide, motivate, and develop other engineers.
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems, or a related field (or equivalent practical experience)

Proven ability to lead and mentor a team of developers, including delegating work, reviewing code, and providing constructive technical feedback.
Strong ownership mindset with the ability to set technical direction and make sound architectural decisions.
Excellent communication skills, able to translate complex technical concepts for both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
Skilled at balancing hands-on development work with team leadership and coordination responsibilities.
Experience facilitating knowledge sharing, onboarding, and upskilling within a development team.
Ability to manage competing priorities across multiple projects while keeping the team focused and on schedule.
Collaborative, solutions-oriented approach to working with business stakeholders, plant operations, and cross-functional IT teams.
Preferred Skills
Experience with SAP S/4HANA integration.
Knowledge of other SAP modules such as SAP PP (Production Planning), SAP QM (Quality Management), or SAP WM (Warehouse Management).
Experience with advanced data analytics and reporting tools.
Prior experience as a technical lead, team lead, or people manager in an SAP manufacturing environment.

Primary Function of Position
We are seeking an experienced Senior BI Analyst to support the design and delivery of Finance reporting, analytics, data products, and process-improvement solutions. Working closely with the Finance Product Owner, this role will serve as an onsite analytical partner to Finance stakeholders and a key link between business, application, data engineering, and reporting teams.
The ideal candidate combines Finance and ERP process knowledge with strong SQL, data analysis, and business intelligence capabilities. Operating at the intersection of business logic and data engineering, you will understand complex business processes, trace data lineage across systems, investigate discrepancies, and translate business needs into clear reporting models and technical requirements. You will design and deliver trusted dashboards, BI data models, operational monitoring, and self-service analytics while evaluating practical automation and AI-assisted analytics opportunities (deep AI/ML engineering experience is not required).
Essential Job Duties
Technical Translation & Requirements Gathering: Partner with the Finance Product Owner and Finance stakeholders to understand business processes, controls, and reporting needs. Translate business needs into functional and data requirements, business rules, report specifications, user stories, and acceptance criteria.
BI Design & Solution Delivery: Design, build, and maintain Finance dashboards, published data sources, BI data models, operational reports, and self-service analytics solutions using Tableau, Power BI, or comparable platforms.
Lineage, Reconciliation & Root-Cause Analysis: Analyze end-to-end processes and data flows across ERP (SAP), CRM, billing, data warehouse, and reporting platforms. Use advanced SQL and analytical tools to reconcile data, validate business rules, investigate discrepancies, and identify root causes.
Performance Tuning & Reporting Reliability: Optimize dashboard usability, query performance, data refresh schedules, metric consistency, and overall reporting reliability.
Delivery Leadership & Governance : Lead assigned workstreams through requirements, solution design, UAT, regression testing, reconciliation, implementation readiness, and stakeholder sign-off. Maintain data definitions, reporting specifications, test evidence, user guides, and governance documentation.
Internal Controls & Quality Monitoring: Support automated monitoring, exception management, data-quality controls, and financially significant/SOX-governed reporting processes.
Cross-Functional & Global Collaboration: Collaborate with application, Data Engineering, Data Science, AI, and platform teams while coordinating and reviewing deliverables across distributed onsite and offshore resources.
Applied AI & Automation Evaluation: Evaluate and support opportunities to implement intelligent alerts, natural-language analytics, AI-assisted analysis, and workflow automation within core Finance processes.
Qualifications
Required Skills and Experience
7+ years of progressive experience in business intelligence, Finance analytics, reporting, business systems analysis, or enterprise data solutions.
ERP & Finance Domain: Experience with SAP or another enterprise ERP platform, including strong understanding of Finance-related processes and cross-system data flows.
Advanced SQL Mastery: Expert-level SQL skills for complex querying, source-to-target reconciliation, data troubleshooting, root-cause analysis, and query performance optimization.
Enterprise BI Platforms: Strong hands-on experience designing dashboards, BI data models, calculated metrics, published data sources, and self-service solutions in Tableau , Power BI , or a comparable enterprise analytics platform.
Data Architecture Fundamentals: Solid understanding of data warehousing concepts, dimensional modeling, semantic layers, data quality, lineage, and visualization best practices.
Delivery & Testing Leadership: Demonstrated experience translating business needs into technical specifications and leading UAT, regression testing, issue resolution, and business-readiness activities.
Communication & Influence: Proven ability to communicate complex business, system, and data topics to technical teams, Finance stakeholders, and senior leadership without direct authority.
Preferred Skills and Experience
Experience with SAP Finance, Salesforce, CPQ/CLM, billing, or revenue-management platforms.
Experience with Snowflake or another modern cloud data platform.
Experience supporting financially significant applications, internal controls, or SOX-governed reporting.
Familiarity with data governance, master data management (MDM), metadata, lineage, and data-quality frameworks.
Exposure to AI-assisted analytics, natural-language querying, intelligent monitoring, Snowflake Cortex, or comparable emerging technologies.
Experience coordinating and reviewing work with distributed onsite and offshore analysts or consultants.
Required Education
Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Information Systems, Business Analytics, Finance, Accounting, Computer Science, Data Analytics, or a related field.
What Success Looks Like
Develops a strong understanding of Finance processes, ERP applications, system integrations, critical data models, and reporting dependencies.
Establishes effective translation and validation practices between Finance stakeholders and technical delivery teams, serving as a trusted onsite partner.
Delivers accurate, intuitive, and performant dashboards and BI solutions that stakeholders trust for day-to-day decision-making and operational reviews.
Independently uses SQL and analytical tools to reconcile data across systems, trace transformations, validate business rules, and identify root causes.
Improves reporting reliability and governance , expanding exception monitoring, data-quality controls, metric consistency, and self-service analytics adoption.
Helps Finance teams adopt automation and AI-assisted analytics where they provide measurable business value and practical process improvements.

Unit testing and code integration efforts to ensure exceptional system reliability and robustness.

Experience working with robotics and system software for complex distributed systems

title: Sr. AI & Automation Engineer, Robotics
description:
It started with a simple idea: what if surgery could be less invasive and recovery less painful? Nearly 30 years later, that question still fuels everything we do at Intuitive . As a global leader in robotic-assisted surgery and minimally invasive care , our technologies—like the da Vinci surgical system and Ion —have transformed how care is delivered for millions of patients worldwide.
We’re a team of engineers, clinicians, and innovators united by one purpose: to make surgery smarter, safer, and more human. Every day, our work helps care teams perform with greater precision and patients recover faster, improving outcomes around the world.
The problems we solve demand creativity, rigor, and collaboration. The work is challenging, but deeply meaningful—because every improvement we make has the potential to change a life.
If you’re ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare , you’ll find your purpose here.
About the Team
The Future Forward organization is Intuitive's advanced concepts group. We explore emerging technologies, prototype next-generation solutions, and build software experiences that shape the future of robotic-assisted surgery. Our research team is building advanced augmented dexterity capabilities for next-generation robotic platforms.
The Role
Our researchers should spend their time on ideas, not on the manual work required to turn those ideas into results on real robots.
As a Senior AI & Automation Engineer, you will build the AI tools, automation systems, integrations, and evaluation capabilities that help researchers and engineers train, test, and evaluate models faster and make better decisions. You'll leverage existing AI technologies while developing new solutions, from agent-driven workflows and AI tooling to the APIs, services, and automation frameworks that support engineering and research activities.
That could mean agents that set up and run experiments, automation workflows that accelerate testing and evaluation, or tools that sort through logs and video to help teams understand failures and improve outcomes. It's a hands-on engineering role that uses AI to improve how physical AI systems are trained and tested. You'll automate that work; you won't design the models themselves. You'll work closely with ML researchers, simulation engineers, and robotics engineers.
What You'll Do
• Build and integrate AI tools, APIs, and agent workflows that automate engineering and research work across the team.
• Automate the training and fine-tuning workflow, from setting up experiments to launching, tracking, and comparing runs, so researchers can reproduce results without hand-built scripts.
• Build automation and integration workflows that help researchers and engineers evaluate new ideas in simulation and on real robots, quickly, reliably, and at scale.
• Design evaluations and experiments that show, with statistical confidence, whether a change is a real improvement.
• Build logging, analysis, and debugging tools that help the team understand results and failures, and that turn robot sessions into data the team can train on.
• Make what you build reliable, secure, and safe to run, with human approval where it matters and responsible use of AI throughout.
• Evaluate emerging AI tools, models, and technologies, and bring in the ones that deliver measurable impact.
• Measure the impact of what you build, document it clearly, and make successful tools part of how the team operates.
What You Bring
We care more about real depth in a few of these areas than shallow coverage of all of them.
• Hands-on work with real robots. You've built testing, automation, or evaluation systems that ran on real robot hardware or other physical systems via software interfaces, not only in the cloud or in simulation.
• AI and automation you've built and put into daily use. You've built LLM-agent workflows, AI tool integrations, copilots, or automation pipelines for real engineering work and measured whether they helped. Be ready to walk us through one: what it did, where it failed, and what you changed.
• Evaluation and experimental rigor. You know how to design experiments and understand the statistics needed to determine whether an improvement is real.
• Strong software engineering. You have 5+ years of software engineering experience.
You write production-quality Python, can read C++, and are comfortable with Linux, CI/CD, Docker, containerized services, APIs, and distributed systems.
Strong candidates often come from robotics, autonomous systems, physical AI, or robot- learning research, and have applied AI tooling to real hardware. You're comfortable working across disciplines in a fast-moving research environment and can explain trade-offs clearly to researchers and engineers alike.
If you don't check every box, we still want to hear from you.
Education
• BS, MS, or PhD in Computer Science, Robotics, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical
Engineering, or a related technical field.
• Advanced degree (MS or PhD) preferred.
Bonus Points
None of these are required. They're signals, not gates, and any one of them is a nice plus.
• Robotics simulation, such as NVIDIA Isaac Sim/Lab or MuJoCo
• Evaluating AI/ML, robotics, or robot-learning systems
• Surgical or medical robotics, including da Vinci Research Kit (dVRK) systems
• ROS 2 or other robot middleware
• Agent frameworks, tool integrations, or MCP servers adopted by engineering teams
• AI assistants, copilots, or productivity tools built for engineers or researchers
• AI applied to scientific, engineering, or research workflows

title: Staff Mechanical Engineer - Future Opportunity
description:
At Intuitive, we are united behind our mission: we believe that minimally invasive care is life-enhancing care. Through ingenuity and intelligent technology, we expand the potential of physicians to heal without constraints.
As a pioneer and market leader in robotic-assisted surgery, we strive to foster an inclusive and diverse team, committed to making a difference. For more than 25 years, we have worked with hospitals and care teams around the world to help solve some of healthcare's hardest challenges and advance what is possible.
Intuitive has been built by the efforts of great people from diverse backgrounds. We believe great ideas can come from anywhere. We strive to foster an inclusive culture built around diversity of thought and mutual respect. We lead with inclusion and empower our team members to do their best work as their most authentic selves.
Passionate people who want to make a difference drive our culture. Our team members are grounded in integrity, have a strong capacity to learn, the energy to get things done, and bring diverse, real world experiences to help us think in new ways. We actively invest in our team members to support their long-term growth so they can continue to advance our mission and achieve their highest potential.
Join a team committed to taking big leaps forward for a global community of healthcare professionals and their patients. Together, let's advance the world of minimally invasive care.
The Staff Mechanical Design Engineer independently owns technically demanding mechanical and electromechanical subsystems for robotic systems. You will lead subsystem architecture and detailed-design decisions, resolve complex multidisciplinary problems, and contribute to integration decisions beyond your assigned subsystem.
This is a hands-on individual contributor role combining mechanical design ownership with technical guidance and mentorship. The role reports to a Manager of Mechanical Design Engineering in New Product Development.
Essential Job Duties
Own subsystem development from concept through verification and design transfer, including mechanical requirements, specifications, design-risk analyses and verification documentation. Support validation activities with the responsible functions.
Lead subsystem architecture decisions. Compare alternatives and justify tradeoffs.
Design precision mechanisms, joints and actuation assemblies. Select and size components such as motors, bearings, transmissions, brakes and sensors based on operating loads, motion requirements and expected life.
Use first-principles calculations and simulation to establish load paths, component margins, structural stiffness, dynamic behavior and fatigue life. Check assumptions and correlate models with test results.
Create and release CAD models, manufacturing drawings and design documentation. Apply GD&T and tolerance analysis to functional interfaces, assembly requirements and inspection.
Build, test, debug and iterate prototypes. Develop test methods and fixtures, investigate failures, and verify corrective actions.
Work directly with suppliers, supplier engineering, sourcing and manufacturing to resolve technical issues, improve DFM/DFA and cost, and prepare designs for transfer.
Collaborate with systems, electrical, controls, clinical, human factors, manufacturing, supplier engineering/sourcing, quality and regulatory partners to resolve requirements and subsystem interfaces.
Lead technical reviews and guide other engineers’ design and analysis approaches. Plan technical work across functions, set priorities, resolve risks and mentor engineers through problem-solving.
Required Skills and Experience
Experience developing robotic or complex electromechanical products in a regulated industry, with demonstrated independent subsystem ownership from concept through design transfer.
Working knowledge of design controls, risk management, verification and validation.
Deep expertise in first-principles mechanics and precision mechanisms, with demonstrated ability to perform stiffness, dynamics and fatigue analysis.
Proficiency in GD&T, tolerancing, materials, DFM/DFA and manufacturing processes.
Experience designing rotary or linear joints, sizing components, and justifying decisions through analysis; integrating actuation and sensing; and collaborating effectively with controls and electrical engineers.
Hands-on prototyping experience, including assembly, testing, debugging, and rapid iterations.
Proficient with CAD, simulation, and PLM tools such as SolidWorks, ANSYS, and Windchill.
Demonstrated technical leadership through design reviews, cross-functional decision-making, stakeholder influence and engineer mentorship.
Experience with risk management activities including FMEA, risk mitigation, and reliability assessments.
Required Education and Training
Required: Typical minimum Bachelor’s degree plus 12 years of relevant experience, or a Master’s degree plus 8 years, or a PhD plus 5 years.
Preferred: Master’s or PhD degree in Mechanical Engineering or a related discipline.
Working Conditions
On-site four days per week in Sunnyvale, CA.
May involve extended periods of computer-based design and analysis work.
Must be comfortable occasionally working in lab environments, including prototype assembly, mechanical testing, and safe use of standard mechanical tools and fixtures.
Must be able to occasionally lift and handle 25 pounds.
Travel: 10%, including occasional visits to supplier and manufacturing sites.
Preferred Skills and Experience
The following skills and experience are not required but represent attributes of an ideal candidate.
Experience developing Class II or Class III medical devices, particularly surgical robotics or medical device capital equipment.
Direct application of standards and documentation frameworks such as ISO 13485, FDA QMSR (21 CFR Part 820), IEC 60601, ISO 14971, and DHF.

As an Area Distributor Manager (ADM) , you will play a critical front-line sales role, driving Kraft Heinz’s Away From Home market share and profitability within a designated geographic territory. This is not a traditional sales role—we are looking for a candidate who takes full ownership of their business, excels at selling solutions, and has a proven track record of winning new business. The ideal candidate will be a leader, influencer, and activator from day one, collaborating with both internal and external stakeholders. This role provides direct contributions to Kraft Heinz’s business growth while offering valuable sales experience that can be leveraged for future career opportunities.
Location: Florida
Essential Functions & Responsibilities
·       Lead the assigned geographic market in the Foodservice Field Sales organization, driving branded market share and profitability in alignment with Kraft Heinz values.
·       Execute all elements of the Foodservice ADM playbook to ensure market success.
·       Develop and implement profitable sales strategies with local distributors, collaborate with brokers and assist operators as needed.
·       Build and maintain strong distributor relationships, supporting local events and initiatives.
·       Drive penetration of high-priority SKUs, focusing on strategic, branded, and profit-oriented products.
·       Identify and manage a pipeline of high-value sales opportunities, collaborating with the Sales Operations Planning team, Finance and Supply.
·       Own the bottom-up sales planning process for your territory, crafting data-driven proposals based on customer needs and market insights.
·       Lead the full sales cycle—from generating interest to securing commitments and closing deals.
·       Meet and exceed assigned revenue targets.
·       Manage trade budgets related to distributors, as well as business and travel expenses.
·       Execute quarterly and annual sales and marketing priorities, including new product launches and limited-time offers.
·       Support the Sales Ops & Planning team by accurately forecasting product demand and submitting Volume Submission Forms (VSFs) for new and renewed business.
·       Establish Joint Business Plans (JBP) with distributors, ensuring regular reviews and execution of agreed-upon actions.
·       Support the Order to Cash process by assisting with distributor orders, resolving invoice discrepancies, and managing payment-related issues.
Expected Experience & Required Skills
·       Bachelor’s degree in business, marketing, sales, or a related field preferred (or equivalent experience).
·       1 to 3 years of sales experience, preferably in foodservice, consumer packaged goods (CPG), or a related industry. Prior experience managing distributor relationships and working with foodservice operators in strongly preferred.
·       Experience in direct sales, account management, or business development within the foodservice or hospitality industry is beneficial.
·       Ability to analyze sales data, market trends, and financial reports to make informed business decisions. Includes the ability to leverage data to track sales performance, plan effectively, and develop winning strategies.
·       Proficiency in building and executing sales plans, including developing joint business plans (JBPs) and forecasting demand.
·       Strong business acumen with the ability to differentiate high-value sales opportunities from less profitable ones.
·       Exceptional verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to present and sell concepts effectively to both internal and external stakeholders.
·       Strong relationship-building skills, with the ability to foster long-term partnerships with distributors, brokers, operators, and key decision-makers.
·       Experience in collaboration cross-functionally with marketing, supply chain, finance, and sales operations teams.
·       Knowledge of supply chain operations, order-to-cash processes, invoice resolution in a foodservice environment.
·       Understanding of pricing structures, rebates, and contracts in a distributor-based sales model.
·       Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook), and CRM tools (e.g., Salesforce).
·       Ability to adapt selling strategies to virtual platforms (MS Teams, Zoom, Google Meet, FaceTime, etc.).
·       Ability to lift up to 50 pounds when needed.
·       Valid driver’s license and ability to meet MVR requirements.
·       Willingness to travel overnight as needed (frequency varies by territory).
Work Environment & Schedule
This is a remote-based role that can be performed from a home office, with travel required based on business needs. The position follows a salaried, exempt schedule, allowing flexibility to meet customer and internal expectations, which may include occasional early mornings, evenings, or weekends. Regular domestic travel within the assigned geographic territory is expected, including overnight trips as necessary. The role requires in-person engagement with customers, distributors, and internal teams to drive business objectives effectively. description:
Job Description
EHS Supervisor
If you’re looking for a role where you can drive higher standards, shape culture, and make a lasting impact on a transformation site, this is that opportunity.
At Kraft Heinz in Fremont, Ohio , the Environmental Health and Safety (EHS) Supervisor is a critical leader at a transformation site with complexity, meaningful operational challenge, and significant opportunity to strengthen how safety, environmental compliance, ownership, and daily execution come to life on the floor. This is a role for someone who wants to build, influence, and lead — not from the sidelines, but in the work, alongside plant leadership, operations, maintenance, quality, and frontline teams.
The right leader will see opportunity in the challenge of helping move the site toward a more prevention-focused, safety excellence culture. In return, this role offers the chance to take on visible leadership, solve meaningful plant-level problems, and grow through the kind of experience that builds real operational credibility.
For the right candidate, this is a chance to step into meaningful leadership at a site with the potential to grow your career and impact— building capability, strengthening culture, influencing site leadership, and helping create a safer, more reliable, and more disciplined operation over time. If you are motivated by challenge, purpose, and the opportunity to lead visible transformation, this role offers the platform to make a lasting impact.
What You’ll Lead
Drive Environmental Health and Safety execution at a transformation site
Lead day-to-day safety and environmental execution across the site to ensure compliance with OSHA, EPA, and Kraft Heinz standards
Partner with plant leadership to identify risk, reinforce expectations, and drive follow-through on the site’s most critical priorities
Build stronger ownership and accountability through visible standards, practical routines, and disciplined execution
Provide hands-on leadership in a plant environment that demands both immediate issue response and long-term culture change
Raise the standard on compliance and risk reduction
Lead routine audits, inspections, and floor-based observations to identify risk and verify compliance
Drive corrective actions to closure with urgency, discipline, and follow-through
Maintain readiness for internal and external reviews through strong documentation, routine management, and operating rigor
Strengthen site execution in ways that protect people, improve compliance, and support stronger overall plant performance
Lead chemical, process, and environmental safety with credibility
Oversee the safe handling, storage, labeling, and use of chemicals tied to production and sanitation processes
Support control of process hazards related to condiment manufacturing, thermal systems, sanitation cycles, and chemical-intensive operations
Lead environmental compliance routines tied to wastewater, waste handling, spill prevention, and required reporting
Help strengthen site control of environmental risks tied to chemical use, acidic waste streams, and older facility conditions
Own incident response, learning, and prevention
Lead investigations for injuries, near misses, environmental events, and significant safety concerns

description:

The Backend Engineer II role independently applies appropriate artificial intelligence tools and best practices throughout the software development lifecycle. The engineer collaborates with internal stakeholders to understand customer and user requirements for a set of features. They create clear and effective test strategies to ensure solution quality and execute thorough test plans. The role involves writing extensible and maintainable code for backend services to minimize defects, reviewing code to assure proper test coverage and adherence to team standards, and implementing debugging tools, tests, logs, and telemetry to validate assumptions. Aim to automate production deployments targeting zero-touch processes when possible. The engineer applies and reviews coding patterns, security risks, and compliance issues to achieve security hardening across product features. This role is in the Messaging Platform team that supports the backend services serving hundreds of millions of enterprise and consumer users across Teams and Copilot.   Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.
Responsibilities
AI-native development
Uses AI tools and practices across the software development lifecycle in a disciplined way, from design and coding through testing, code review and incident investigation. Takes responsibility for every AI-generated change: reviews it fully and applies the right tooling and processes with minimal guidance.
Coding
Writes, and reuses where it makes sense, extensible, maintainable code for messaging services and features with minimal supervision. Considers how easy it is to diagnose, how reliable it is and how well it handles concurrency, ordering and idempotency, with few defects. Knows when code is ready to ship.
Uses debugging, tests, logs and telemetry to check assumptions before issues reach production. Runs incident retrospectives to find root causes, puts repair items in place and prevents recurrence, using least-access principles and protecting privacy throughout.
Reviews product and test code promptly for correctness, test coverage, security risks, compliance issues and maintainability. Uses automated code analysis tools and coaches peers through useful review feedback.
Design
Reviews and comments on architecture proposals for globally distributed messaging systems, such as ingestion, fan-out, storage, sync and notification, with technical leadership from others. Explores design options and lays out the trade-offs of each, and owns some design decisions.
Helps make sure designs meet requirements for performance, scalability, resiliency and cost of goods sold (COGS) at the scale of billions of messages a day. Upholds Microsoft security, privacy and compliance standards.
Contributes to design documents. Identifies dependencies and downstream interactions across the platform (storage, identity, Substrate, Teams and Copilot clients and services) and works with partner teams where dependencies and validation overlap.
Creates clear test strategies that prevent regressions. Runs test plans that include security testing, including negative cases, with minimal supervision. Designs for testability and uses AI tools for test automation.
Engineering excellence
Contributes to deployment automation for complex messaging features, aiming for zero-touch deployment. Validates code in non-production and production-like environments.
Applies security best practices and "security as code" invariants. Contributes to security review standards, security deployment gates and scanners, and security monitoring. Works with security partners on threat models, premortems, breach drills and incident response, and makes sure AI safety features are in place for AI-powered capabilities.
Works with partner teams before go-live so end-to-end testing, live-site coverage, scalability, performance and DRI escalation paths are in place.
Follows the processes for security, privacy, safety and accessibility. Checks for visible evidence of compliance, such as audit trails, and keeps up with global and local regulations that affect messaging data, such as retention, eDiscovery, data residency and sovereign clouds.
Applies well-established and secure design practices to build services that scale to customer demand and meet performance expectations and security commitments.
Stays current on ways to improve availability, reliability, efficiency and observability at scale. Shares knowledge through learning sessions, flags engineering tool gaps, and reuses open-source or internal code responsibly.
Implement
Works with TPMs and stakeholders to review work items, carry out project and release plans, break large work into estimated pieces and raise issues that could cause delays. Makes sure security, privacy and compliance protections are accounted for in planning.
Makes sure all code is flighted (released behind feature flags) so production incidents can be mitigated quickly. Calculates capacity with failover, backup and restore, and disaster recovery in mind, plans for efficient operation after launch, and contributes to rollback plans.
Follows safe deployment practices across rings and regions with managerial guidance. Monitors dependency versions so only the latest secure versions are deployed, and contributes to infrastructure that lets developers test private builds in production-like environments.
Runs experiments with feature flags and flighting. Works with Data Science and PM to define success and guardrail metrics.
Reliability and supportability
Contributes logging, instrumentation and telemetry on performance, reliability, availability, usage and safety. Builds dashboards and alerts that improve issue detection and security investigation, and considers the privacy impact of every telemetry change.
Keeps the live service running during on-call rotations. Mitigates issues quickly and securely with the minimum required permissions, and escalates appropriately. Improves troubleshooting guides (TSGs), wikis, tests and telemetry to make on-call better.
Acts as DRI (designated responsible individual). Monitors for degradation, downtime or interruptions, responds within the service-level agreement (SLA), keeps stakeholders informed and escalates to the right owners.
Understand user requirements
Works with PM, privacy and security experts, and tech leads to understand customer requirements. Brings customer insights and continuous feedback loops into designs and fixes, using quantitative signals (usage, performance) and qualitative ones (accessibility, globalization), and speaks up for customers' security and privacy needs.

Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science or related technical field AND 2+ years technical engineering experience with coding in languages including, but not limited to C#, or Java OR equivalent experience.

It also means setting up repeatable modernization approaches that other teams can adopt without disrupting customers.

You will prototype solutions to hard problems so teams can reduce risk before they commit to an architecture. You will develop the standards and golden paths that define effective pro-code development in ITP, and build or promote tools, including AI-assisted engineering tools, that make engineers more productive. description:
Overview
Security is one of the most critical priorities for our customers in a world of growing digital threats, regulatory scrutiny, and estate complexity. Microsoft Security aspires to make the world safer by empowering every user, customer, and developer with a security cloud that delivers end-to-end, simplified protection. The Microsoft Security Research (MSecR) conducts security research at the intersection of offense, defense, and intelligence. AI is now everywhere: organizations and people across every industry are adopting large language models, copilots, and autonomous agents, and these systems bring a brand-new attack surface that can be manipulated, misused, and exploited in ways traditional software cannot. In Microsoft Security, we protect AI from these attacks. We are looking for a Senior Security Researcher and a Principal Security Researcher who combines a real security background with a deep, hands-on understanding of how modern AI works and how it breaks. You will help execute and conduct AI attacks through simulations, using what you find to make AI safer and to inform our security products so they protect customers better. This role is for someone who wants to shape how AI attacks are simulated and defended at scale. You will set methodology, build tooling, influence product direction, and drive innovation in attacking and defending AI systems (Security for AI). Responsibilities
As a Senior AI Security Researcher, you will:
Lead the design and execution of simulations aimed at making AI safer, conducting realistic AI attacks whose findings inform our security products and help them protect customers more effectively.
Develop and execute hands-on attacks against AI systems, including: 1) Direct prompt injection and jailbreaks that bypass system prompts, safety instructions, and alignment.
2) Indirect (cross-domain) prompt injection (XPIA), where malicious instructions are hidden in untrusted content the model consumes: documents, web pages, emails, tickets, code, and RAG sources.
3) Multi-turn, crescendo, and social-engineering style attacks that steer a model toward unsafe behavior over a conversation.
4) Multimodal injection through images, audio, and files that carry hidden instructions.
5) Guardrail, content filter, and safety-system bypass, including encoding, obfuscation, and adversarial phrasing.
6) Sensitive data exfiltration and leakage, including system prompt and grounding-data disclosure and cross-tenant or cross-session leakage.
7) Agentic and tool-use abuse: excessive agency, confused-deputy attacks, unsafe autonomous actions, and manipulation of tools, plugins, and connected systems. 8) Data and model attacks: training-data and RAG poisoning, model extraction, model inversion, membership inference, and adversarial examples / evasion.
Build scalable AI red teaming tooling and automation (custom attack harnesses and evaluation frameworks) to generate attack variations, run large evaluations, and continuously test AI systems as they change.
Partner with product, engineering, Responsible AI, and detection teams to translate findings into mitigations: better system prompts, input and output filters, grounding controls, agent guardrails, and detections.
Evaluate the effectiveness of AI defenses (detections, safety classifiers, filters, and monitoring) and provide strategic recommendations to close gaps.
Conduct deep research into emerging AI attacker techniques and map them to frameworks such as MITRE ATLAS and the OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications.
Deliver executive-level briefings, technical reports, and prioritized, actionable recommendations.
Act as a technical leader: shape AI simulation methodology, mentor team members, and drive long-term innovation in Security for AI.

Identify risks involving data quality, bias, variance, methodological limitations, and model assumptions.

description:
About the Team

OpenAI’s mission is to ensure that artificial general intelligence (AGI) benefits all of humanity. Achieving this goal requires more than cutting-edge research—it also demands deep, durable engagement with policymakers, institutions, industry leaders, and communities shaping the future of AI around the world.

The Global Affairs team leads this engagement globally, building trusted relationships with governments, regulators, civil society organizations, academic institutions, and strategic partners. By bringing external perspectives into OpenAI—and helping communicate OpenAI’s priorities outward—we support thoughtful governance frameworks, responsible standards, and public understanding of AI technologies.

We work closely across research, product, legal, communications, partnerships, and go-to-market teams to anticipate emerging issues, shape proactive engagement strategies, and advance OpenAI’s mission internationally.

 

About the Role

OpenAI believes that access to AI tools and training should expand opportunity. We’re looking for an Academy Partnerships Lead to manage and strengthen the partner relationships that support OpenAI Academy’s programming. 

This person will work with nonprofits, educational institutions, community organizations, industry associations, and other partners to bring practical AI learning to the communities they serve. They will serve as the primary point of contact for a portfolio of Academy partners, translating shared goals into clear plans and supporting delivery from onboarding through evaluation and expansion.

You’ll play a critical role in helping partners deliver successful hands-on learning experiences and build the capacity to sustain AI education within their own organizations and communities.


Key Responsibilities

Partnership Development & Management

 - Build and manage relationships with partners supporting Academy Jams and our Community Trainer Program. 

 - Translate partnership commitments into clear scopes, responsibilities, timelines, and success measures.

 - Assess partner recruitment, facilitator capacity, and delivery readiness; guide onboarding and implementation.

 - Align partner expectations with Academy priorities, resources, and delivery capacity.

Program Strategy & Execution

 - Manage contractors and delivery partners supporting assigned Jams and train-the-trainer programs.

 - Own partner participation in the train-the-trainer program, from readiness and commitments through implementation, performance, and expansion.

 - Work closely with Academy program, curriculum, and instructional teams to connect partners with appropriate content, training, and support.

 - Develop playbooks, onboarding materials, and implementation guidance that make partner delivery consistent and repeatable.

 - Evaluate partner performance and feedback; recommend improvements, renewals, expansion, or exits.

External Engagement

 - Represent OpenAI Academy in partner meetings, workshops, and community convenings.

 - Identify opportunities to reach new audiences and deepen successful partnerships.

 - Synthesize partner needs and insights to inform Academy content, delivery models, and strategy.

 - Contribute to briefing materials, presentations, and updates on partnership progress and impact.

 

You might thrive in this role if you have:

 - Experience managing partnerships and programs within education, nonprofit, community, workforce development, or public-sector environments.

 - Strong relationship-management and stakeholder-engagement skills.

 - Experience executing initiatives involving multiple organizations, from planning through implementation and evaluation.

 - Excellent communication and project management abilities, including managing competing priorities across a portfolio of partners.

 - Experience supporting workshops, facilitator networks, train-the-trainer programs, or other partner-led learning models.

 - The ability to translate broad partnership goals into practical delivery plans and clear commitments.

 - Familiarity with adult learning, AI literacy, or community education.

 - A commitment to expanding access to opportunity through technology and education.

 - Comfort operating in fast-paced, ambiguous environments and building processes as programs grow.

We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products.
